items.body:
## Bug Description

Hermes Desktop's Computer Use provider picker does not persist or recognize the only available provider, `cua-driver (background)`. The provider card shows `Ready`, but clicking the white `Use this backend` button returns to the same CTA after the provider configuration is refreshed or reopened.

The underlying cua-driver runtime works correctly; this is a Desktop/provider-selection state bug.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop → **Capabilities** → **Tools**.
2. Select **Computer Use (macOS/Windows/Linux)**.
3. Expand `cua-driver (background)`.
4. Click the white **Use this backend** button.
5. Refresh the provider panel or leave and reopen the Computer Use details.

## Expected Behavior

The sole available provider should remain marked as active, or the activation CTA should be hidden/disabled once the backend is ready. The selection should survive a refresh and a Desktop restart.

## Actual Behavior

The provider card continues to show **Use this backend** after clicking it. The UI briefly treats the provider as selected, then the state reverts when the config is read again.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.1 arm64
- Hermes Desktop: v0.20.1 (+70), commit `3f9150e`
- cua-driver: 0.19.3
- Repository: `NousResearch/hermes-agent`

## Error Output

No visible error is shown. `hermes computer-use doctor` passes:

- MCP session active
- Accessibility granted
- Screen Recording granted
- AX reachable
- Background AX capture succeeds

## Additional Context

The runtime defaults to CUA via `HERMES_COMPUTER_USE_BACKEND` with a default of `cua`, so Computer Use itself remains usable despite the broken picker state.

Source-level suspected cause:

- `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/toolset-config-panel.tsx` sends `PUT /api/tools/toolsets/{name}/provider` and optimistically marks the provider active.
- The `computer_use` category defines only `cua-driver (background)` with a `post_setup` hook and no provider/backend config marker.
- `hermes_cli.tools_config._write_provider_config()` has no `computer_use` provider persistence branch.
- `hermes_cli.tools_config._is_provider_active()` falls through to `False` for this provider, so a subsequent refresh removes the active state.

Possible fixes: treat the ready sole CUA provider as active, add an explicit `computer_use.backend` config key and active-provider resolver, or remove the redundant activation CTA for this single fixed backend.

items.title: openrouter/auto (routing model ID) makes Hermes runtime fragile at init — model_metadata.py GET /models hang/timeout

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
**Severity:** bug (cron/CLI unreliable with OpenRouter Auto Router)

**Repro:**
- provider=openrouter (built-in), OPENROUTER_API_KEY set.
- `hermes chat -q "PONG" --provider openrouter -m openrouter/auto`
  (cron jobs use the same Hermes runtime path.)

**Expected:** Hermes resolves the routing model, sends prompt, returns response. OpenRouter Auto Router is a real documented endpoint. Direct API call (POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions, model:"openrouter/auto") returns HTTP 200 and routes to e.g. deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 (verified 5/5 requests, 0 rate-limit headers, ~$0.000009/req).

**Actual:** Hermes runtime is fragile with this model ID.
- model_metadata.py fetches model metadata (GET /models) to resolve context length for `openrouter/auto`.
- `openrouter/auto` is a routing alias with NO fixed catalog entry, so the metadata fetch is unreliable: in one independent test it hung/timed out (~30s, ConnectionTimeout -> KeyboardInterrupt before any prompt was sent); in another it eventually succeeded but took ~35s.
- Provider itself resolves fine (no "Unknown provider") — the failure is purely in the metadata init phase, not config/key/provider.

**Independent verification:**
- Direct OpenRouter API model:"openrouter/auto": 5/5 HTTP 200, routes to deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731, no 429, ~$0.000009/req.
- Pinned model `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` works through Hermes cleanly (has catalog metadata, no init delay) — confirms the issue is specifically the routing-model ID lacking metadata handling.

**Suggested fix:** in model_metadata.py, treat unknown/routing model IDs (anything not in the catalog, or IDs containing `/auto`, `/:online`, etc.) with a fallback context length instead of blocking/slow-fetching GET /models; or skip the metadata fetch for provider=openrouter when the model ID is a known routing alias.

**Environment:** Hermes Agent (Nous Research), provider openrouter built-in, OPENROUTER_API_KEY present. Observed 2026-08-15.

items.title: Skill install/update fails when skills/ directory is a symlink or junction (Windows)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
**Describe the bug**

When the skills directory is a symlink/junction pointing elsewhere (e.g. `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes\skills` → `D:\hermes-data\skills` via `mklink /J`), `hermes skills install <slug> --force` passes quarantine and the security scan, then fails at the final step:

```
Installation blocked: 'D:\hermes-data\skills\<slug>' is not in the subpath of 'C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes\skills' OR one path is relative and the other is absolute.
```

This is the raw `ValueError` from `Path.relative_to()` (Python 3.9–3.12 raises instead of returning `False` on non-subpaths).

**Root cause**

In `tools/skills_hub.py`, `install_from_quarantine()`:

- `install_dir` comes from `_resolve_lock_install_path()`, which calls `Path.resolve()` — this follows the junction and returns the real path (D:).
- `_skills_dir()` returns `HERMES_HOME / "skills"` **unresolved** (the C: junction path).
- `install_path=str(install_dir.relative_to(_skills_dir()))` mixes a resolved path with an unresolved one → `ValueError`.

A sibling occurrence exists in `hermes_cli/skills_hub.py`, `do_install()`:

```python
c.print(f"[bold green]Installed:[/] {install_dir.relative_to(SKILLS_DIR)}")
```

**Side effects observed**

1. `shutil.move` executes *before* the failing `relative_to()` — files land on disk but `record_install` is never reached, so the lock file ends up with no `content_hash` entry.
2. Without `content_hash`, `hermes skills check` reports `update_available` forever, while `hermes skills update <name>` prints "No updates available" (name filter mismatch). The user is stuck in a check/update loop.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. On Windows: `mklink /J C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes\skills D:\hermes-data\skills`
2. `hermes skills install clawhub/pdf-image-text-extractor --force`
3. Observe "Installation blocked" despite the scan passing.

**Proposed fix**

Resolve both sides before computing the relative path:

```python
install_path=str(install_dir.relative_to(_skills_dir().resolve())),
```

```python
c.print(f"[bold green]Installed:[/] {install_dir.relative_to(SKILLS_DIR.resolve())}")
```

**Environment**

- Hermes Agent v0.20.0, Windows 10
- Python 3.11.15
- skills dir relocated via directory junction

items.title: Session-hygiene compression timeout writes the shared failure cooldown and stops the in-agent compressor

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Bug Description

The gateway session hygiene uses an inactivity watchdog of 30 s (`_hyg_timeout_seconds`, default at `gateway/run.py:17073`). A local model cannot meet this limit. The summarization call must read all of the conversation before it sends the first token. Before that token there is no progress that can extend the window.

This endpoint gives approximately 2,440 tokens per second on the prefill (from `/metrics`: 6,203,456 prompt tokens in 2,543 s). Thus a prompt of approximately 290,000 tokens needs approximately 120 s before the first output. The watchdog stops the operation at 30 s each time.

That alone is only a tuning problem. The defect is the next step. After the timeout, `_record_hygiene_cooldown` (`gateway/run.py:237`) writes the failure to `sessions.compression_failure_cooldown_until`. The in-conversation compressor reads the same column (`agent/context_compressor.py:2160`) and shows it as `cooldown:<n>` through `_compression_block_reason`. That compressor has an idle budget of 120 s (`DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`), which is sufficient on the same hardware.

Thus a path that cannot succeed stops a path that can. The block is 300 s and increases three times to `_HYGIENE_COOLDOWN_MAX_SECONDS` (3600 s). The session continues to increase in size until the user finds the problem.

## Evidence

```
WARNING gateway.run: Session hygiene compression for session <id> made no progress
for 30.0s (total wait 30.1s, ceiling 600.0s); continuing without compression
WARNING gateway.run: Session hygiene auto-compress failed:
```

The operation stops at 30.1 s, but its own ceiling is 600 s. The ceiling has no effect, because the idle window stops the operation first.

The user then sees this message from the in-agent path:

```
Context is over the compression threshold (~290,497 tokens >= 196,608) but compression is currently blocked (cooldown:300)
```

Issue #79540 shows the same subsystem with a fast provider: `still streaming after 30s (last progress 0.0s ago) - extending wait (ceiling 600s)`. There the stream started, thus the idle window continued to extend and the compaction finished in 75-187 s. The failure in this report occurs when the prefill time is more than the idle budget. That is the usual condition for a self-hosted model on a long session.

## Difference from other issues

- #78981 - the opposite condition on the agent path. That path waits to the 600 s ceiling and does not stop. It does not use hygiene or the shared cooldown.
- #79540 - hygiene starts again because of the message-count floor. The compaction there succeeds.
- #74136 (closed) - that change made the hygiene cooldown durable in this column. The durability is correct. The effect on the other path looks unintentional.

## Suggested fix

1. Limit the hygiene failure cooldown to hygiene. A watchdog timeout in the pre-agent pass must stop only that pass. The in-conversation compressor has its own budget and its own failure sequence (60/300/900 s), and it must be permitted to try. This part is independent of the timeout value.
2. Make a difference between "the prefill is not complete" and "the summary model has a fault". The documentation of the cooldown gives recovery from HTTP 429 and transient summary-model faults as its function. A watchdog timeout is not evidence of that condition.
3. Optional: calculate the first-token wait from the prompt size, or use `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` as the minimum default. The idle clock starts before the prefill. Thus a 30 s budget is not possible for a sufficiently long prompt, and the condition of the provider has no effect on this. Note the disadvantage: hygiene runs before the agent and stops the reply, thus a larger default increases the delay that the user sees. For this reason fix 1 is more important than fix 3.

## Environment

Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), checkout `212e84176d`, Linux, gateway (Telegram), local vLLM through `provider: custom` (Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, 262,144 token window). `compression.hygiene_timeout_seconds` is not set, thus the default of 30 s applies.

items.title: [Bug]: hermes chat --provider <custom> ignores provider default_model when a global model.default is set

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Bug Description

When a user adds a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint under `providers:<name>` (or `custom_providers:`) and sets `default_model`, running `hermes chat --provider <name>` does **not** use that `default_model`. Instead Hermes sends the **global** `model.default` value as the `model` field in the API request, while still routing to the custom `base_url`.

The custom server (e.g. llama.cpp) usually ignores the model id and answers anyway, so the failure is *silent*: Hermes thinks it is talking to `tencent/hy3:free` (or whatever the global default is) when it is actually talking to the local model.

Side effects:
- The **context compressor is initialized with the global `model.context_length`** (e.g. 262144) instead of the real model's context (e.g. 65536).
- The **agent loop / tool guards key off the wrong model identity**, which changes agentic behaviour (observed: multi-step tool loops behave differently).
- `--verbose` shows `provider=custom base_url=http://gmk.lan:9931/v1 model=tencent/hy3:free` — i.e. correct endpoint, wrong model string.

**Workaround that works:** pass the model id explicitly on the command line: `hermes chat --provider <name> -m "<real-model-id>"`. With `-m` set, routing and `context_length=65536` are both correct.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a global default set, e.g. `config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   model:
     default: tencent/hy3:free
     provider: nous
   providers:
     gmk-lan:
       name: GMK Local
       base_url: http://gmk.lan:9931/v1
       api_key: not-needed
       default_model: /home/user/.lmstudio/models/unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-GGUF/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
   ```
2. Start a llama.cpp / OpenAI-compatible server on `http://gmk.lan:9931` serving the `default_model` above (single-model server; it ignores the requested id).
3. Run: `hermes chat --provider gmk-lan -q "Reply with exactly: PONG" -v`
4. Inspect the startup log line: `OpenAI client created ... provider=custom base_url=http://gmk.lan:9931/v1 model=tencent/hy3:free`

## Expected Behavior

`--provider gmk-lan` should resolve the model to the provider entry's `default_model` and initialize the context compressor with that model's real context length, **regardless of the global `model.default`**.

## Actual Behavior

`--provider gmk-lan` alone sends `model=tencent/hy3:free` (the global default) to the custom endpoint, and initializes context length from the global `model.context_length`. The `-m <id>` flag is required to get correct behaviour.

## Root-Cause Analysis (code pointers)

- `cli.py` ~line 4676 initializes `self.model` from the **global** `model.default`/`model.model` at construction:
  ```python
  _raw_default = (_model_config.get("default") or _model_config.get("model") or "")
  ```
- `hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py` lines 149–163 only copy the provider's `default_model` into `self.model` when `self.model` is empty / equals the provider slug / equals `runtime.get("name")`:
  ```python
  runtime_model = runtime.get("model")          # the gmk-lan default_model
  should_use_runtime_model = (
      not self.model or
      self.model == self.provider or
      self.model == runtime.get("name")
  )
  if should_use_runtime_model:
      self.model = runtime_model
  ```
  Because `self.model` is already the non-empty global default, the condition is `False` and `runtime_model` (the custom `default_model`) is **never applied**.
- The runtime resolver (`hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py` line 760) *does* return `result["model"] = entry.get("default_model", "")` for the provider entry — but that value is discarded by the mixin's guard above.

**Suggested fix:** in `cli_agent_setup_mixin.py`, when an explicit `--provider` (or `requested_provider`) is set, prefer the resolved provider's `default_model` over the global `model.default` (the explicit provider choice should win). The `should_use_runtime_model` guard should also treat "provider was explicitly requested" as a reason to adopt `runtime_model`.

## Supporting evidence

Verbose startup with `--provider gmk-lan` (NO `-m`):
```
OpenAI client created ... provider=custom base_url=http://gmk.lan:9931/v1 model=tencent/hy3:free
Context compressor initialized: model=tencent/hy3:free context_length=262144 ...
```

Verbose startup with `--provider gmk-lan -m <gemma id>` (workaround):
```
OpenAI client created ... provider=custom base_url=http://gmk.lan:9931/v1 model=/home/user/.../gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
Context compressor initialized: model=.../gemma-... context_length=65536 ...
```

**Affected version:** Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13)

items.title: [Bug]: Gateway /loop deadlocks after empty or incomplete wakeup response

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Bug Description

A gateway `/loop` can deadlock permanently when a loop wakeup turn ends with an empty/incomplete model response. The loop remains persisted as `active` with `awaiting_response=true`, so the gateway watcher skips it forever.

Observed with a self-paced loop whose current cadence was one minute. Tick 1 completed normally. Tick 2 performed its tool calls, but the Codex response remained incomplete after three continuation attempts and the gateway produced a zero-character final response. No subsequent ticks fired.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Hermes through the Telegram gateway.
2. Create a loop, for example: `/loop monitor a condition every minute and notify when complete`.
3. Allow a wakeup tick to reach a model failure that produces an empty final response (in this instance: hidden-reasoning-only incomplete response after continuation retries).
4. Run `/loop status` or inspect persisted loop state.

## Expected Behavior

A failed or empty wakeup turn should release `awaiting_response` and re-arm the loop—possibly with retry/backoff—or explicitly stop it with an error notice. The loop watcher must not become permanently wedged.

## Actual Behavior

The loop remains `active` but stuck as `wakeup running`. Future watcher scans skip it indefinitely because `awaiting_response` remains true.

Redacted log timeline:

```text
13:13:18 loop wakeup #1 injected
13:13:41 tick #1 completed; response sent
13:14:48 loop wakeup #2 injected
13:14:57 tools completed
13:15:16 response ready ... response=0 chars
13:15:16 Suppressing hidden-reasoning-only incomplete gateway turn:
         Codex response remained incomplete after 3 continuation attempts
[No further loop wakeups]
```

Persisted status afterwards:

```text
↻ Loop (active, self-paced, currently 1m, 2/100 budget, wakeup running)
```

## Affected Component

- Gateway
- Agent Core

## Messaging Platform

Telegram

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13)
- Commit: `f0c222c73dff282784dcf2cd91a14a32035a2ccd` (`origin/main` at time of reproduction)
- macOS 26.3.1
- Hermes runtime Python 3.11.15
- Provider/model: OpenAI Codex / GPT-5.6

Full `hermes debug share` was intentionally not uploaded because it may include private configuration and unrelated recent logs. The relevant log excerpt above is redacted.

## Root Cause Analysis

In `gateway/run.py`, loop completion is reached through `_post_turn_loop_completion(...)`, which calls `LoopManager.complete_tick(...)` and clears/schedules the in-flight tick.

However, the post-turn hook is guarded by a non-empty final response check:

```python
if _final_text.strip():
    ...
    await self._post_turn_loop_completion(...)
```

When the gateway returns an empty response after an incomplete model turn, that hook is skipped. The loop therefore retains `awaiting_response=true`.

The watcher then intentionally ignores it:

```python
if state.awaiting_response or now < state.next_due_at:
    continue
```

This creates a permanent deadlock rather than a transient failed tick.

## Proposed Fix

On every gateway turn exit associated with an in-flight loop wakeup, ensure the tick is finalized even when `final_response` is empty:

- call `complete_tick("")` with an explicit failure/retry policy, or
- call `abandon_tick()` and schedule the next retry/backoff,
- ideally emit a bounded diagnostic notice only if retries are exhausted.

Add a regression test covering a loop wakeup whose agent result has an empty final response and verify that `awaiting_response` becomes false and a subsequent tick can fire.

items.title: Termux: make native pkg install/upgrade the first-class Android path

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes currently has several separate Termux/Android installation and update failure modes, but they share a distribution-level root problem: a stock rolling Termux environment is not a normal manylinux host, and installing/rebuilding Hermes' complete Python/native dependency graph at end-user install/update time is fragile.

This issue is intended as an **umbrella for a first-class native Termux package-manager path**, not as a duplicate of each individual compatibility bug.

A complete native proof path now exists and is usable today through a contributor-operated signed APT repository. The proposed upstream end state is to move the canonical build/provenance side into **NousResearch-owned CI/releases** and make native `pkg` installation the preferred Termux path, with PRoot retained as a compatibility fallback rather than the default answer.

## User-visible problem

On current Termux, users can encounter different failures depending on the rolling Python/dependency state:

- #71331 / #76288 — Termux's rolling Python can be newer than Hermes' supported Python range.
- #73126 — `uv`/wheel compatibility behavior can differ on Android/Termux.
- #40328 — PRoot has additional cross-filesystem/build-isolation problems.
- #75148 — update/venv health logic can probe the wrong interpreter/layout.
- #83680 — locally built Rust extensions such as `cryptography` can load incorrectly under Android/Bionic; #85985 addresses that specific overlay.
- #85972 — another example of a dependency that imports but fails at runtime on Android.

Fixing these individually is still useful, but the recurring pattern is that the user's phone is being asked to resolve/build a desktop-oriented Python/native graph at install or update time.

## Why native `pkg` should be the preferred Termux UX

`proot-distro` is valuable as a compatibility fallback because it supplies a conventional Linux userspace, but it adds another userspace/process/filesystem translation layer. For Hermes, which performs substantial Python imports, subprocess/tool execution, filesystem work, package management and sometimes browser/Node operations, that overhead is especially noticeable on older or lower-powered Android devices.

A native Android/Bionic package avoids that layer and lets Termux's package manager own upgrades and rollback semantics:

```text
pkg install hermes-agent
pkg upgrade hermes-agent
```

This also means `hermes update` should not mutate files owned by dpkg/APT. PR #85606 now contains the corresponding `apt` install-method semantics and directs an APT-managed install to `pkg upgrade hermes-agent`.

## Working path available today (proof/distribution path)

This is **contributor-operated, not an official NousResearch repository**. It is useful today and proves the native packaging design, but it does not replace the provenance handoff requested by maintainers.

On a fresh aarch64 Termux install:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adybag14-cyber/termux-python/main/scripts/setup_apt_repo.sh | bash
pkg install hermes-agent
```

Updates are then ordinary package-manager updates:

```bash
pkg update
pkg upgrade hermes-agent
```

The same repository currently exposes side-by-side Python packages (`python3.9` through `python3.14`), `uv`, and `wrangler` without taking ownership of the generic `python`/`python3` aliases.

Repository signing fingerprint:

```text
EAD24A2124EFA7393A78B7B14699F966313F7A6B
```

Current Hermes package:

```text
hermes-agent 0.20.1+termux2
```

Immutable release:
https://github.com/adybag14-cyber/termux-hermes/releases/tag/hermes-agent-termux-0.20.1-20260815.2

Package SHA-256:

```text
b76c50b850c1031e172f22b86cc10d351b3a66f0a4938bc3a4634aa772f919d2
```

## Validation already running

The package is built in a pinned native aarch64 Termux userspace, inspected, then installed into a **second clean Termux container** before the release is allowed to publish:

https://github.com/adybag14-cyber/termux-hermes/actions/runs/31883241280

After publication, a separate CI job enables the **live signed APT repository** and installs Hermes entirely through `pkg install hermes-agent`; it checks the APT install marker, updater behavior, and native-extension imports:

https://github.com/adybag14-cyber/termux-hermes/actions/runs/31883428394

Both are green.

The supporting signed-APT/Python repository also has a native ARM regression proving that `pkg install python3.13` does not install or replace Termux's generic `python` package.

## Distribution/provenance design of the proof path

The current proof setup deliberately separates build, download and signing responsibilities:

1. GitHub Actions builds/tests release artifacts.
2. GitHub immutable releases lock the release tag/assets after publication.
3. An unprivileged Oracle-hosted poller checks the public GitHub releases and requires GitHub's published SHA-256 digest before staging a `.deb`.
4. The poller has no signing key and no sudo capability; its systemd unit is sandboxed (`NoNewPrivileges`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, restricted writable path).
5. A separate root-owned local publisher validates package identity/architecture, signs `Release`/`InRelease`, verifies the resulting signature, and atomically switches the public snapshot.
6. The private APT signing key never enters GitHub Actions.

Non-secret server configuration is tracked here:
https://github.com/adybag14-cyber/termux-python/tree/main/server

Both `termux-python` and `termux-hermes` have repository-level immutable releases enabled.

## Important governance boundary

This is the same boundary discussed in #67163 and #85606:

**The contributor-operated APT repository proves that native `pkg install` works, but it should not become the canonical trust root for Hermes.**

The canonical Hermes Termux runtime/wheelhouse/package should be built and released by **NousResearch-owned CI**. PR #85606 intentionally remains draft/blocked until that ownership/provenance handoff exists.

## Proposed upstream end state

1. Create a NousResearch-owned Termux artifact/build repository (or equivalent workflows in a Nous-owned repository).
2. Move the existing CPython/runtime and Android/Bionic wheelhouse builders into Nous-owned CI.
3. Build on native ARM where possible and pin the Termux userspace/image inputs.
4. Publish immutable releases with checksums/provenance/attestations.
5. Build a `hermes-agent` aarch64 `.deb` from an exact Hermes source revision and the verified native dependency set.
6. Publish through a NousResearch-controlled signed APT repository (or contribute an accepted package to the appropriate Termux repository if maintainers prefer that route).
7. Teach the installer/docs to prefer native Termux package installation when running in Termux.
8. Keep `proot-distro` documented as a compatibility fallback for unsupported architectures/dependencies rather than the preferred normal path.
9. Keep APT installs package-manager-owned: `hermes update` must direct users to `pkg upgrade hermes-agent` rather than mutate dpkg-owned files.
10. Gate each release with a fresh native aarch64 Termux test that adds the repository and runs `pkg install hermes-agent` from scratch.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fresh supported aarch64 Termux can install Hermes without PRoot and without compiling Hermes' native Python dependency graph on the phone.
- [ ] `pkg install hermes-agent` starts Hermes successfully.
- [ ] `pkg upgrade hermes-agent` is the supported update path for that install type.
- [ ] Native-extension smoke tests cover at least `cryptography`, `pydantic_core`, `cffi`, `psutil`, Pillow, PyYAML, `jiter` and `rpds`.
- [ ] Generic Termux `python` is not replaced just to satisfy Hermes' currently supported Python ABI.
- [ ] Canonical artifacts are built/released from NousResearch-owned CI with immutable versioned artifacts and verifiable checksums/provenance.
- [ ] PRoot remains available as fallback, but is not required for the normal supported native aarch64 path.

## Related implementation

- #85606 — native install/update slice, including `apt` install-method/update semantics.
- #67163 — original broader Termux work and the maintainer provenance/splitting discussion.
- #85540 — narrow-terminal TUI slice.
- #85604 — Termux Desktop/browser-host slice (separate security decision).

I can help transplant the already-tested builder/package/repository tooling into whatever NousResearch-owned repository/layout maintainers choose.

items.title: `_configured_provider_matches` double-counts a single `providers.<slug>` endpoint → `/model <name>` fails with "declared by multiple configured providers"

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility

items.body:
## Summary

When a self-hosted / OpenAI-compatible endpoint is configured under the v12+ `providers:` dict (e.g. `providers.local-qwen`), switching to its model with a **bare model name** — `/model <model>` in a chat, or the dashboard chat model switch — fails with:

> `'<model>' is declared by multiple configured providers (custom:<name>, <slug>). Re-run with --provider <slug> to choose which one to use.`

…even though the model is declared by **exactly one** on-disk provider. Selecting *with* an explicit provider (`/model <model> --provider <slug>`, or the dashboard Models picker which sends the provider) works fine. Only the bare-name path is affected.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13)
- A single `providers.local-qwen` entry pointing at a local `llama-server` (`http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1`); **no** `custom_providers:` list entry.

## Reproduce

`~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
```yaml
providers:
  local-qwen:
    base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1
    model: my-model
    models:
      my-model: {}
model:
  provider: some-default-provider   # anything other than local-qwen
  default: some-default-model
```

In a chat: `/model my-model` →
`'my-model' is declared by multiple configured providers (custom:local-qwen, local-qwen). Re-run with --provider <slug>…`

There is only one declaration.

## Root cause

`switch_model()`'s configured-provider match step, `_configured_provider_matches()` in `hermes_cli/model_switch.py`, scans **two** collections that the caller (`hermes_cli/inventory.py:load_picker_context()`) builds as:

```python
user_providers  = cfg.get("providers")                  # the providers: dict
custom_providers = get_compatible_custom_providers(cfg)  # a merged list
```

`get_compatible_custom_providers()` (`hermes_cli/config.py`) **merges the `providers:` dict into the returned list** via `providers_dict_to_custom_providers()`, so a single `providers.<slug>` endpoint appears in **both** collections. `_configured_provider_matches()` then keys them differently:

- `user_providers` branch → `matches["<slug>"]` (bare, e.g. `local-qwen`)
- `custom_providers` branch → `matches["custom:<name>"]` (e.g. `custom:local-qwen`)

The custom branch's only dedup guard can never fire for this case:

```python
slug = f"custom:{name}"
if slug in matches:   # matches holds the *bare* "local-qwen", never "custom:local-qwen"
    continue
```

→ the one endpoint is counted twice, `switch_model()` sees `len(cfg_matches) > 1`, and raises "declared by multiple configured providers" (the `# Step d.5` block).

## Suggested fix

Skip `custom_providers` entries whose `provider_key` (set by `providers_dict_to_custom_providers()`) already matched a `user_providers` slug — i.e. the entry is just the `providers.<slug>` dict re-emitted:

```diff
     if isinstance(custom_providers, list):
         for entry in custom_providers:
             if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                 continue
+            # A providers.<slug> entry re-emitted by
+            # get_compatible_custom_providers() was already matched above under
+            # its bare slug; counting it again as "custom:<name>" double-counts a
+            # single endpoint and yields a spurious "declared by multiple
+            # configured providers".
+            provider_key = entry.get("provider_key")
+            if isinstance(provider_key, str) and provider_key in matches:
+                continue
             name = entry.get("name")
             if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip():
                 continue
             slug = f"custom:{name}"
```

This preserves genuine collisions (a *separate* legacy `custom_providers:` entry with a different `provider_key` declaring the same model still counts).

## Impact / workaround

Any user who registers a local/OpenAI-compatible endpoint the documented way (`hermes model` → Custom endpoint → written to `providers.<slug>`) cannot `/model <bare-name>` to it. Workaround: always name the provider — `/model <model> --provider <slug>` or the dashboard Models picker. (The related default-provider-mismatch path also surfaces as an `HTTP 400` / "model does not exist" misroute to the configured default provider when the model isn't paired with its provider.)

Related: #45006 (the configured-provider routing `_configured_provider_matches` implements).

items.title: fix(gateway): orphan-reap on desktop startup kills independently-started gateway instances on Windows

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Bug

Every time the Hermes desktop app (or `hermes serve` / `hermes dashboard`) starts
on Windows, `_reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()` in `hermes_cli/gateway.py` kills
**every** running gateway process it finds, regardless of how that gateway was
started. This includes gateways started by a Scheduled Task boot trigger, a
LogonTrigger, or background `hermes gateway run` sessions.

### Evidence — three independent deaths, same <10s cause

| Date | Gateway death | Desktop backend start | Delta |
|------|--------------|----------------------|-------|
| 12 Aug | 13:25:49 (last heartbeat) | 13:25:54 (`server started`) | **5s** |
| 13 Aug | 18:56:30 (last heartbeat) | 18:56:37 (`Mounted plugin API routes`) | **7s** |
| 14 Aug | 18:30:30 (last heartbeat) | 18:30:40 (`Desktop cron scheduler started`) | **10s** |

Each death occurs **within 10 seconds** of a desktop serve-backend start.
The mechanism: `web_server.py` line 242 calls
`_reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()` on `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` startup, which
calls `find_gateway_pids()` → `_scan_gateway_pids()` — this matches ANY
running process whose command line contains `-m hermes_cli.main gateway run`
within the current profile, and sends SIGTERM → SIGKILL. **No config flag,
env var, launch arg, or skip path can prevent it.**

### Impact

- **Boot-triggered gateway killed**: a gateway started pre-login via a
  Scheduled Task BootTrigger runs for 2–5 minutes until the user opens the
  desktop app, then is silently killed. Messages sent during that window
  may be lost — see the companion issue on cold-boot restarts dropping the
  pending-update queue for the mechanism and proof.
- **Duplicate instance prevented, but at the wrong level**: the reap was
  designed to prevent two gateway instances from running on the same profile,
  but it assumes every extra gateway is from a leftover zombie — not that
  one might be the *intended* instance started by a boot trigger.
- **Silent outage, no recovery path**: the reap logs no message to the user
  or to the killed gateway's log. The user only discovers the gateway is down
  when Telegram replies stop. The probe (if configured) restarts the gateway
  on its next 5-minute tick — incurring 2–5 minutes of downtime every
  desktop launch.

## Root Cause

The reap was added to handle the case where a gateway process survived its
terminal session (e.g., orphaned after an SSH disconnect on Linux). On Windows,
it fires on every desktop-app startup because `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` is set
unconditionally when `web_server.py` initialises. The check does not
distinguish between:
- A leftover zombie that survived its parent's death (the intended target)
- A healthy gateway started by a Scheduled Task or boot trigger (the
  **intended** instance that should be left alone)

## Proposed Fix Options

### Option A: Gate the reap by parent PID (recommended)

Skip the reap for any gateway whose parent PID is not the current desktop
backend's own child. A boot-triggered or scheduled-task gateway has
`wscript.exe`/`cmd.exe` (via schtasks) as its parent — not `hermes serve` —
so it is never mistaken for an orphan.

On Linux, read `$PPID` or `stat /proc/$pid/status`. On Windows, check the
process's parent PID (`wmic process where "ProcessId=$pid" get ParentProcessId`)
and only reap when the parent is the shell/backend that launched the desktop
process.

### Option B: Make the reap opt-in

Replace the unconditional reap with a config setting under `gateway:` in
`config.yaml`:

```yaml
gateway:
  reap_orphans_on_startup: false  # default false; true preserves old behaviour
```

Existing users who depend on the reap for cleanup can enable it; new users
with boot triggers won't lose their gateway on every desktop launch.

### Option C: Track ownership through the desktop supervisor

Alternative to Option A: only reap gateway processes that were **spawned by
the same desktop backend's own supervised subprocess mechanism** — track the
backend's spawned-child list and reap only those. Heavier than Option A (needs
an ownership record), but the most precise if the parent chain is unreliable
(e.g. intermediate shells).

## Delivery

- `hermes_cli/gateway.py` or `web_server.py`: modify `_reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()`
  to gate on parent PID / config flag
- `gateway/run.py`: nothing — no change to gateway lifecycle
- `config.yaml` schema: add `gateway.reap_orphans_on_startup` (if Option B)

## Testing

- **Manual**: start gateway via `hermes gateway run`, then start `hermes serve`.
  Verify gateway process survives (no kill within 10s). Repeat with boot-trigger
  gateway (Scheduled Task BootTrigger).
- **Regression**: verify that a genuinely orphaned gateway (simulate by starting
  a gateway in a subprocess and letting the parent die) IS still reaped, so
  the cleanup function isn't entirely removed.
- **E2E**: the upstream test suite should verify that `hermes serve` does not
  kill gateway processes that were started independently.

## Notes

- Measured example: in one observed case the boot-triggered gateway was
  killed **~47 seconds after login** — the boot trigger fired at boot and the
  desktop app started ~47s after login. The probe recovered it in ~3 minutes.
  The gap varies with when the desktop app starts; it is not a fixed value.
- The same reap mechanism exists in `gateway/run.py`'s `_reap_self_on_start`
  for the gateway itself. That one is correct — it prevents duplicate gateways
  on the same profile by checking `lockfile + PID match`. The desktop-backend
  reap is broader and should be narrowed.

items.title: Telegram adapter can hang indefinitely on connect — the connect-attempt timeout never fires

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
Body:

**Environment**
- Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13), commit `30c469b15313711d47c45e7175d6ef5c8437f1ed`
- Self-hosted via the provided `docker-compose.yml` (gateway + dashboard services, `network_mode: host`)
- Ubuntu host, Docker Compose v5.1.4

**Symptom**

On `gateway run` startup, the log prints:

```
WARNING [Telegram] Discovering Telegram API fallback IPs via DNS-over-HTTPS…
WARNING [Telegram] Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…
```

...and then nothing further. No timeout message, no retry, no error, no successful connection — for 7+ minutes straight (confirmed via `ps`: the process is alive, ~2% CPU, not crashed, just never progresses past "attempt 1/8").

Ruled out network connectivity as the cause: `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}' https://api.telegram.org` from the same host/container returns `302` in ~0.55s.

**Suspected root cause**

In `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` (~line 4469), the connect attempt is wrapped as:

```python
await _await_with_thread_deadline(
    self._app.initialize(),
    timeout=_init_timeout,
    # On timeout the initialize() task is abandoned without
    # awaiting its cancellation (it may be wedged in a
    # shielded scope). Best-effort release the half-built
    # app's httpx client/connection pool so it isn't leaked
    # across the retry ladder ...
    on_abandon=lambda app=self._app: _shutdown_abandoned_app(app),
)
```

`_init_timeout` defaults to 30s (`HERMES_TELEGRAM_INIT_TIMEOUT`). The surrounding `except asyncio.TimeoutError` handler is supposed to log `"Connect attempt %d/%d timed out after %.0fs — retrying in %ds"` and retry (up to 8 attempts). In my case this handler never fires — the code's own comment already anticipates this failure mode ("it may be wedged in a shielded scope"), and that's what I believe I hit: `self._app.initialize()` gets stuck somewhere that isn't actually cancellable by the deadline wrapper, so the whole connect sequence wedges forever instead of timing out and retrying/failing.

**Workaround**

Rolling back to commit `49d7481dfb9622d40c19ef9f78294e2a6a8355e5` (v0.16.0, predates the DNS-over-HTTPS fallback discovery step) connects normally. I haven't bisected the exact commit that introduced the regression — happy to help narrow it down if useful.

**Not yet tried**

Lowering `HERMES_TELEGRAM_INIT_TIMEOUT`/`HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` — didn't seem worth trying since the issue looks like the timeout mechanism isn't firing at all, not that it's set too high.

items.title: warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars() false-positive on local backend (no TERMINAL_CWD in .env)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

On a stock **local-backend** CLI install, Hermes prints a startup warning claiming `TERMINAL_CWD=...` was "found in .env" and is deprecated — even though the value does **not** exist in `~/.hermes/.env` (or the shell environment). There is nothing for the user to migrate; the suggested fix would actually break the intended behavior.

## Reproduction

1. Local-backend setup: `terminal: { backend: local, cwd: "." }` in `config.yaml`; no `TERMINAL_CWD` in `~/.hermes/.env` or the shell.
2. Run `hermes` (CLI/TUI) from any working directory.
3. The deprecation banner appears on startup:

```
⚠ Deprecated .env settings detected:
  ⚠ TERMINAL_CWD=/abs/path/to/launch/dir found in .env — this is deprecated.
  Move to config.yaml instead:  terminal:\n    cwd: /your/project/path
  Then remove the old entries from ~/.hermes/.env
```

Verified the env var is **not** in the `.env` file, not in the shell, and not in any parent process's `/proc/PID/environ` — it is injected into `os.environ` by Hermes itself.

## Root cause

`warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` reads **process environment**, not the `.env` file:

```
hermes_cli/config.py:2189  terminal_cwd_env = os.environ.get("TERMINAL_CWD")
hermes_cli/config.py:2208  if terminal_cwd_env and not config_has_explicit_cwd:
```

But the local-backend CLI path populates `os.environ["TERMINAL_CWD"]` itself when it resolves the `cwd: "."` placeholder to the launch directory:

```
cli.py:647  if effective_backend == "local":
cli.py:648      terminal_config["cwd"] = os.getcwd()
cli.py:656  "cwd": "TERMINAL_CWD",   # env_mappings
```

So `os.environ["TERMINAL_CWD"]` is present (set by Hermes, not the user), and `config.yaml`'s `terminal.cwd` is `.` (a placeholder), which trips the guard at `config.py:2208`. The banner then misattributes the value to `.env`.

The codebase already recognizes this distinction. The doctor path checks the **on-disk `.env`** file explicitly to avoid this exact false positive:

```
hermes_cli/doctor.py:436  # Deprecated env vars (checked in the .env file, not process env, so config→env
hermes_cli/doctor.py:437  # bridges like terminal.cwd → TERMINAL_CWD do not false-positive).
hermes_cli/doctor.py:480-481  *env_map* should come from the on-disk `.env` ... not ``os.environ``,
                               so bridged runtime vars do not trigger false positives.
```

`warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` is the outlier — it checks `os.environ`.

## Impact

- Misleading: directs the user to edit `.env` (nothing to remove) and to hard-code an absolute path into `config.yaml`, which would break the intended "run from the current directory" behavior of `cwd: "."`.
- No functional effect — the terminal tool works correctly.

## Suggested fix

Make `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` inspect the **on-disk `.env` file** instead of `os.environ`, consistent with `doctor.collect_deprecated_env_vars()`. A shared helper returning the on-disk env dict (e.g. from `env_loader`) would let the doctor and this warning read the same source of truth.

Alternative (less invasive): skip the warning entirely when `terminal.backend == "local"`, since local cwd resolution always bridges `cwd: "."` → `os.getcwd()` and is documented expected behavior.

## Files / lines

- `hermes_cli/config.py:2182-2226` — `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()`
- `cli.py:639-658` — local-backend cwd → `TERMINAL_CWD` bridge
- `hermes_cli/doctor.py:436-490` — the already-correct on-disk `.env` check

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (git checkout at `c9a806e`)
- OS: Linux
- `config.yaml`: `terminal: { backend: "local", cwd: "." }`

items.title: Local/custom provider (Ollama): agent never emits real tool_calls for MCP tools — narrates fabricated results instead, or returns empty content

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
**Environment:** Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13), macOS, Ollama local (`provider: custom`, `base_url: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`), HA-MCP server connected via `hermes mcp add` (HTTP transport, 11 tools, connectivity confirmed via `hermes mcp test`).

**Bug:** When asked to use an MCP tool (e.g. `ha_search`), the agent either (a) fabricates plausible-looking but entirely fake tool output / fake shell sessions instead of calling the real tool, or (b) returns empty final content after 4 retries with `tool_call_count: 0`.

**Tested and ruled out:**
- Not a model-capability issue: reproduced identically across 5 models/vendors (`qwen3.5:9b`, `mistral-nemo:latest`, `llama3.1:8b`, `gemma4:e4b`, `hermes3:8b`).
- Model *is* capable: calling Ollama's raw `/v1/chat/completions` directly with a minimal `tools` schema gets a correct `tool_calls` response from `hermes3:8b` (`finish_reason: "tool_calls"`).
- Not toolset overload: pruning built-in toolsets (8,200→3,092 input tokens via `-t`) didn't change the outcome — still 0 tool calls.
- Not Ollama concurrency: set `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=4` and restarted Ollama fresh — same failure, still 0 tool calls / empty content.
- MCP server itself is healthy: calling `ha_search` directly via raw JSON-RPC against the MCP endpoint returns correct real data.
- Already on latest version (`hermes update --check` → up to date).

Looks related to #6559 and #21811 but reproduces without any other concurrent Ollama load (checked `ollama ps` / `lsof -i :11434` at time of failure — no contention).

**Repro:**
```
hermes -z "Call the ha_search tool with query 'pool' and report exactly what it returns." 
```
with any MCP server configured under `provider: custom`.
