items.body:
Set up Bedrock with an API key via `hermes model` > Bedrock > API Key. Every request then fails:

```
401 - {'error': {'code': 'invalid_api_key', 'message': 'Invalid bearer token', ...}}
```

The key is fine, here I am using the same endpoint with the same token with curl:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK" \
  https://bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws/v1/models
# 200, 55 models
```

What happens: `_model_flow_bedrock_api_key` in `hermes_cli/model_setup_flows.py` saves the bearer token to `OPENAI_API_KEY` and sets `model.provider: custom` plus `model.base_url` to the mantle endpoint. At runtime the bare-custom branch in `hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py` only reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` when the host matches openai.com, which is the gate from #28660. `bedrock-mantle.*.api.aws` doesn't match, `_host_derived_api_key()` derives nothing useful either, so `api_key` falls through to the literal `"no-key-required"`. That string is what goes out as the bearer token.

I think this broke when #29606 landed (2026-05-21). The wizard's `OPENAI_API_KEY` approach predates it and nothing reconciled the two; that PR's review doesn't mention Bedrock.

Not the same as #28156. That one was `provider: bedrock` and the AnthropicBedrock SDK. This is the `provider: custom` + mantle path.

Separately, `hermes doctor` reports Bedrock as OK throughout, because it probes the control plane with `list_foundation_models()` instead of the endpoint that's configured. Filing that on its own.

Ubuntu, Python 3.11, hermes v0.18.2, us-east-1, long-term API key from the Bedrock console.

items.title: Desktop 0.20.1: headless serve catch-all 404 breaks plugin REST routes for profiles without plugin enabled + boot-time dashboard token scrape regression

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### Environment
- Hermes Agent 0.20.1 (core `a90d5369f`), Windows 11, Desktop app (Electron)
- User plugin `meeting-intelligence` with a `dashboard/plugin_api.py` FastAPI router (deployed to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\plugins\meeting-intelligence`, listed in `plugins.enabled` in the primary config.yaml)

### Symptom
After updating to 0.20.1, a desktop plugin page that calls `ctx.rest('/meetings')` fails with:

```
Error invoking remote method 'hermes.api': Error 404:
{"error":"Headless backend (hermes serve): web UI disabled — use `hermes dashboard` for the browser UI."}
```

`desktop.log` additionally shows, for **every** profile backend at boot:

```
[boot] could not read served dashboard token (Hermes backend for profile "presale"): 404: {"error":"Headless backend (hermes serve): web UI disabled ..."}
```

### Analysis

Two separate problems, both introduced alongside `f0f8c84d1` ("feat(cli): make hermes serve a real headless backend"):

**1. Boot regression: Desktop still scrapes a dashboard token that `serve` can never serve.**

`hermes serve` sets `HERMES_SERVE_HEADLESS=1` (`hermes_cli/main.py:10700-10703`), and `mount_spa()` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:16510-16525`) installs a catch-all `GET /{full_path:path}` returning 404 `web UI disabled`. But the Desktop still calls `adoptServedDashboardToken(...)` which fetches `<baseUrl>/` and parses the injected token:

- `apps/desktop/electron/dashboard-token.ts:52-69`
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:8260-8264` (pool backends)
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:8604-8607` (primary backend)

That request is guaranteed to 404 on every `serve` backend. The exception is caught and the spawn token retained, so today it's noise + one wasted round-trip per profile per boot — but it's a contract violation left behind by the headless split.

**2. Misleading 404 body: absent plugin router is indistinguishable from "headless UI disabled".**

Plugin API routers are mounted *before* `mount_spa` (`web_server.py:17803-17813` → `_mount_plugin_api_routes()` at `:17689`), so a *mounted* plugin route is reachable on a headless backend. However, `_mount_plugin_api_routes` gates user plugins on the **per-profile** `plugins.enabled` allow-list (`web_server.py:17719-17740`). When a pool/profile backend runs without the plugin enabled, its `/api/plugins/<name>/*` routes don't exist, and the request falls through to the headless catch-all — surfacing to the user as "web UI disabled", which points debugging entirely in the wrong direction (it looks like a headless/desktop-mode bug, not a plugin-not-enabled-in-this-profile fact).

The standalone desktop plugin frontend loads globally (registered via `ctx.register` for all windows) but its REST backend exists only per-profile — so switching the active profile to one without the plugin enabled breaks the page with the misleading error above.

Live verification on this machine: primary `serve` backend returns **401 Unauthorized** on `GET /api/plugins/meeting-intelligence/meetings` (route mounted), while a backend whose profile lacks the plugin in `plugins.enabled` returns the headless 404 body.

### Proposed fixes

**Fix A (core, minimal):** skip the dashboard-index token scrape for real `serve` children — only the legacy `dashboard --no-open` fallback needs it.

```diff
--- a/apps/desktop/electron/main.ts
+++ b/apps/desktop/electron/main.ts
@@
-  const authToken = await adoptServedDashboardToken(baseUrl, token, {
-    childAlive: () => child.exitCode === null && !child.killed,
-    label: `Hermes backend for profile "${profile}"`,
-    rememberLog
-  })
+  // `serve` has no index.html by contract. Only the legacy fallback launches
+  // `dashboard --no-open`, whose injected index token remains the authority.
+  const authToken = backend.args.includes('serve')
+    ? token
+    : await adoptServedDashboardToken(baseUrl, token, {
+        childAlive: () => child.exitCode === null && !child.killed,
+        label: `Hermes backend for profile "${profile}"`,
+        rememberLog
+      })
```
(same branch at the primary-backend call site)

**Fix B (core, DX):** make route-absence diagnosable. Options:
- In headless mode, restrict the catch-all to non-`/api/*` paths, letting FastAPI's native 404 (`{"detail":"Not Found"}` / "No such API endpoint") surface for API calls; or
- Have the catch-all detect `/api/` prefixed paths and return `404 {"error":"No such API endpoint", "hint":"plugin router not mounted — is the plugin in plugins.enabled for this profile?"}`.

**Fix C (product, optional):** let the plugin host expose which plugin REST routers the active backend actually mounted (e.g. via a capability in the plugin context), so a standalone plugin page can render a proper "backend unavailable for this profile" state instead of a generic error.

### Repro
1. Install a user plugin with a `dashboard/plugin_api.py` router; add it to `plugins.enabled` of the default profile only.
2. Start Desktop 0.20.1, open the plugin page → works.
3. Switch active profile to one whose config.yaml does not enable the plugin → plugin page shows `Error invoking remote method 'hermes.api': Error 404: ... web UI disabled`.
4. `desktop.log` also shows `could not read served dashboard token ... web UI disabled` for every profile at boot.

Full audit trail with file:line evidence: `C:\Work\hermes\meeting\audit\FINDINGS.md` (local; happy to attach if useful).

items.body:
# Bug Report — Hermes Desktop: subagent timeout "computing…" göstergesi takılı kalıyor

**Repo:** NousResearch/hermes-agent
**Sürüm:** v0.20.1 (packaged, Windows 10)

---

## Title

Desktop: subagent timeout leaves "computing…" / "1 Alt ajan" indicator stuck until app restart

## Repro

1. `delegate_task` ile tarayıcı (`browser_exec`) kullanan bir subagent başlatın.
2. Subagent 600s timeout olduğunda backend `subagent.complete (status=timeout)` döner.
3. Arayüzde "1 Alt ajan" paneli ve "(u_u) computing…" göstergesi **kapanmaz**, restart'a kadar takılı kalır.

## Analiz

- `apps/desktop/src/store/subagents.ts` timeout'u doğru `'failed'` yapıyor (`asStatus` satır 63-65, `timeoutSummary` satır 133-137) — yani subagent *row* durumu doğru.
- Sorun **ana stream'in** "computing/thinking" status-tail'inin, delegasyon timeout'unda terminal sinyali almadığı için kapanmaması (backend→frontend event boşluğu).
- Ayrıca `browser_exec` subagent'i başlattığı Chrome'u (`--remote-debugging-port=9222`) timeout'ta öldürmüyor → yetim process (RAM yiyor).

## Ek not

- `hermes update` bu sorunu ÇÖZMEZ — bekleyen commit (`165c889e5 fix(cli): Kitty keyboard protocol`) alakasız.

## Geçici önlemler

- Subagent'lere `browser_exec` yerine `web_extract_plus` kullandırmak (daha az timeout).
- Takılı panel için: pencereyi kapatmak değil, **tray'den tamamen Quit** (in-memory state temizlenir).

---

*(Bu rapor 2026-08-15 tarihinde, gerçek bir timeout senaryosu üzerinden hazırlanmıştır.)*

items.title: Gemini thinking exhausts max_tokens budget, aborting after 4 continuations

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
Related: #83915

## Symptom
Gemini models with thinking enabled (e.g. gemini-3.7-flash, thinking level high/ultra) fail with:
`Response remained truncated after 4 continuation attempts`

## Root cause
Gemini bills thought tokens against `maxOutputTokens` / `max_tokens`. With the global Hermes cap at 4096, thinking consumes the entire budget on the first request, leaving 0 content tokens. Every continuation repeats this, so the loop deterministically aborts after 4 attempts.

## Fix
Raise the effective output cap to the 65,535 ceiling when thinking is enabled, on both paths:
- `agent/gemini_native_adapter.py`: `_effective_gemini_max_output_tokens()` — native `maxOutputTokens`
- `agent/transports/chat_completions.py`: `_raise_gemini_thinking_max_tokens()` — chat-completions `max_tokens`

Explicit caps without thinking are preserved as-is.

## Tests
`tests/agent/test_gemini_native_adapter.py`, `tests/agent/transports/test_chat_completions.py` — 60 passed.

items.title: /status shows wrong provider: billing_provider is last-write-wins, not majority provider
items.body:
## Bug: `/status` displays wrong provider when multiple fallback providers are used in a session

### Symptom

`/status` showed:
```
Model: z-ai/glm-5.2 (nous)
```

But `z-ai/glm-5.2` is served by **NVIDIA NIM** (`https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/`), not Nous. Nous doesn't even have this model.

### Verified state

Session `20260815_131325_b864e6e2`:

```
sessions table:
  model: z-ai/glm-5.2
  billing_provider: nous                    ← wrong
  billing_base_url: https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1/   ← wrong

session_model_usage table (correct per-provider breakdown):
  model=z-ai/glm-5.2,          billing_provider=nvidia,  api_calls=48
  model=meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct, billing_provider=nvidia, api_calls=1
  model=upstage/solar-pro4:free, billing_provider=nous,    api_calls=6
```

The session used three providers in sequence:
1. Primary (opencode-zen/deepseek) → failed (rate-limited)
2. Fallback slot 1: `z-ai/glm-5.2` on **nvidia** → 48 API calls (served the entire conversation)
3. Fallback slot 2: `upstage/solar-pro4:free` on **nous** → 6 API calls (brief fallback during a transient GLM failure)

### Root cause

`gateway/slash_commands.py` resolves the provider for `/status` display as:
1. Live agent's `agent.provider` (not available when agent isn't running)
2. `session_row.get("billing_provider")` ← falls back to this
3. Config default

`billing_provider` in the `sessions` table is a **single field** overwritten on every API call via `agent/conversation_loop.py:3889`:
```python
agent._session_db.queue_token_counts(
    ...
    billing_provider=agent.provider,
    billing_base_url=agent.base_url,
    ...
)
```

This is **last-write-wins**. The last 6 API calls were on Nous (solar-pro4:free), so `billing_provider` was overwritten to `nous`. But `model` was also overwritten to `upstage/solar-pro4:free` on those calls — yet `/status` showed `z-ai/glm-5.2`, not solar-pro4:free.

This means the `model` and `billing_provider` fields in the sessions table can become **inconsistent with each other** — they may come from different API calls at different times, combined into one display line. The `model` field shows the model from one call; `billing_provider` shows the provider from a different call.

### Why it's different from #75535 and #77521

- **#75535**: `billing_provider` is NULL → falls to config default. (This bug: `billing_provider` is non-NULL but stale.)
- **#77521**: Status snapshots stale/historical values and wrong "agent running" state. (This bug: the values are freshly wrong — correct at write time but misaligned with each other.)

### Proposed fix

Option A (minimal): When building the `/status` display, read from `session_model_usage` instead of `sessions.billing_provider`. Match the displayed model to its provider in the per-model table. The `session_model_usage` table already correctly tracks `model`, `billing_provider`, and `billing_base_url` per-provider-per-model.

Option B (structural): Stop using a single `billing_provider` field in `sessions` for sessions that span multiple providers. Either store the **majority** provider (by API call count) or store the **primary** provider (the one that served first/most), not the last one.

Option C: Read `gateway_runtime.provider` from `sessions.model_config` (as proposed in #75535) — but this would show the *last active* provider, which has the same last-write-wins problem.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.1
- Session: `20260815_131325_b864e6e2`
- Fallback chain: primary=opencode-zen/deepseek-v4-flash-free → nvidia/z-ai/glm-5.2 → nous/upstage/solar-pro4:free

### Evidence

```
$ sqlite3 ~/.hermes/state.db "SELECT id, model, billing_provider, billing_base_url FROM sessions WHERE id='20260815_131325_b864e6e2'"
20260815_131325_b864e6e2|z-ai/glm-5.2|nous|https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1/

$ sqlite3 ~/.hermes/state.db "SELECT model, billing_provider, billing_base_url, api_call_count FROM session_model_usage WHERE session_id='20260815_131325_b864e6e2'"
z-ai/glm-5.2|nvidia|https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/|48
meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct|nvidia|https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/|1
upstage/solar-pro4:free|nous|https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1/|6
```

items.title: macOS Desktop: /auth/native/authorize request omits provider parameter, causing Unknown provider: ''

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
**Environment:** Hermes Desktop, macOS (Electron/Chrome build), self-hosted gateway with `basic` + `self-hosted` OIDC providers configured (`auth_flows: ["cookie", "native_pkce"]`)

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Configure a self-hosted OIDC provider (`HERMES_DASHBOARD_OIDC_ISSUER` / `HERMES_DASHBOARD_OIDC_CLIENT_ID`) alongside Basic Auth on the backend.
2. On macOS, open Hermes Desktop → Settings → Gateway → Remote gateway → enter the gateway URL → click Sign in.
3. App opens the system browser to `/auth/native/authorize` with a valid `code_challenge`, `code_challenge_method`, `redirect_uri`, and `state` — but **no `provider` parameter is included in the query string**.
4. Backend correctly rejects the request with `{"detail":"Unknown provider: ''"}`.
5. App shows a generic `Desktop boot failed: Could not reach the remote Hermes gateway while refreshing its WebSocket ticket. Try reconnecting.` and loops indefinitely on automatic retry — it never surfaces the actual 400-level auth rejection to the user, only a misleading reachability-style error.

**Example URL captured from app logs (redacted state/challenge):**
```
https://<gateway>/auth/native/authorize?code_challenge=<...>&code_challenge_method=S256&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A<port>%2Fcallback&state=<...>
```
Note the absence of a `provider=` parameter.

**Expected behavior:** The generated authorize URL should include `provider=self-hosted` (or whichever provider is selected/configured as default), matching what a standard browser-based login flow correctly sends to the same backend.

**Confirmed workaround:** Manually appending `&provider=self-hosted` to the logged authorize URL and completing the OAuth flow in a regular browser tab (instead of relying on the app's built-in in-app browser/flow) successfully completes login, and the resulting callback to `127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` is correctly picked up by the app's local listener — confirming the rest of the PKCE/local-callback flow is implemented correctly and this is isolated to the missing `provider` parameter.

**Additional notes:**
- This appears intermittent — quitting and relaunching the app has, on at least one occasion, "fixed" it without any config change, suggesting a possible race condition in how the login URL is constructed relative to when the app finishes loading its available-providers list from `/api/status`.
- The generic "Could not reach the remote Hermes gateway" retry-loop message is misleading in this scenario — the actual failure is a 400-level authentication rejection (bad request), not a network reachability issue, and the app does not currently distinguish between the two for the user.
- Backend correctly advertises both providers via `/api/status` → `"auth_providers": ["basic", "self-hosted"]` at the time of reproduction, ruling out a server misconfiguration.

items.title: Background review fork: token usage invisible to telemetry, prompt not configurable, tightly coupled to core

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
> **Edit (2026-08-15):** figures in this issue were re-measured after the initial filing; the original numbers overstated volume. Methodology is now stated inline. Original text is in the edit history.

## What happens

After every turn, `spawn_background_review` (`agent/background_review.py`) forks an auxiliary agent loop in a daemon thread. The fork replays a digest of the conversation (recent turns verbatim, older turns truncated) and may write skills or memories. The loop runs up to 16 iterations per fork. There is no notification to the user, no entry in the session transcript, and — as detailed below — no usage record in any queryable store.

On long-session or multi-profile hosts this fork becomes a significant share of total token consumption. We measured it after noticing provider quota draining on days when no one was chatting.

## Why it is hard to notice

1. **Fork API calls are logged under the parent session's ID.** The `API call #N: model=... in=... out=...` lines in `agent.log` carry no `thread=` tag; the `thread=bg-review` tag exists only on separate lifecycle lines. Attributing usage to the fork requires correlating by model string, which only works when the auxiliary model is not used by anything else on that profile.

2. **`session_model_usage` does not capture it — and captures less than assumed overall.** On one profile, for the same model and window, the table holds 18 rows / 3.4M tokens where `agent.log` shows 1,472 calls / 127M input. The fork's calls appear in the table not at all. The log's `API call` lines are, as far as we can tell, the only complete per-call record — and nothing rolls them up.

3. **The fork cannot terminate on "nothing to save."** The review prompt instructs: *"Be ACTIVE — most sessions produce at least one skill update... A pass that does nothing is a missed learning opportunity, not a neutral outcome."* Both forks we sampled in detail ran to `max_iterations_reached(16/16)` — exploring the skill store (`skill_view`, searches, ~28 tool executions), attempting writes, absorbing validation rejections, and being cut off mid-output. The iteration cap, not a conclusion, is what stops the loop.

## Measured impact

v0.20.1, Linux, zai provider. Attribution method: on these profiles the auxiliary model (`glm-4.5-flash`) has exactly one configured consumer (`auxiliary.background_review`; vision/web-extract/skills-hub/approval route to other models), so filtering log lines by model is exact. Corroborated by spawn counts: calls-per-spawn ratios come out 7.9–10.0, consistent with the loop cap. `in=` is cache-inclusive (the log line prints `cache=X/Y` alongside).

**Profile A (heavy daily use), 6-day window** (bounded by log rotation; lifetime burn is higher):
- 82 forks, 644 LLM calls
- **34.4M input / 0.4M output**, ~90% served as cache reads
- Main conversation loop in the same window: 127M input → **the reviewer burned ≈21% of what the conversation itself used**

**Profile B (mostly idle chat), 18-day window:**
- 114 forks, 1,135 calls, **65.5M input / 0.6M output** (~91% cache reads)
- Main loop: 98.7M input → **fork ≈66% of main-loop input**, on a profile that was doing very little

**Profile C (light use), 17-day window:** 46 forks, 459 calls, 33.7M input / 0.2M output.

Per call the fork averages ~53K input; ~8–10 calls per fork event. Whether the ~90% cache-read share is discounted depends entirely on provider and plan; Hermes surfaces the split nowhere, so operators cannot reason about it.

## The three gaps

1. **Accounting.** Fork usage should be persisted (e.g. `session_model_usage` rows with `task='background_review'` and thread id) and appear in usage reports. A completion log line per fork (`calls=N, in=…, out=…, result=none|skill|memory`) would make the cost visible at the point where it is incurred. More broadly: if `agent.log` is the only complete per-call record, a rollup of it (or equivalent persistence) would fix attribution for auxiliary tasks generally.

2. **Configurability.** `_SKILL_REVIEW_PROMPT` is a module constant — but the source reads it via `getattr(agent, "_SKILL_REVIEW_PROMPT", default)`, which reads like an anticipated override seam that was never exposed. Operators cannot make the reviewer conservative, cap its iteration budget, or redefine "worth saving." Suggested keys: `auxiliary.background_review.{prompt_file, max_iterations}`.

3. **Decoupling.** The review strategy is welded into core. Moving it behind a swappable component (as memory providers are) would let operators replace or remove it without touching core code. Short of that, a documented `background_review.enabled: false` — today the only off-switch is the emergent side effect of zeroing the nudge intervals (below).

## Workaround for operators (current versions)

```bash
# Measure (usage lines hide under the parent session id; filter by aux model,
# include rotated logs):
zcat -f ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/logs/agent.log* \
  | grep -E "API call #[0-9]+: model=<your-aux-model>" \
  | grep -oE "in=[0-9]+" | grep -oE "[0-9]+" \
  | awk '{s+=$1} END {printf "input tokens: %.1fM\n", s/1e6}'

# Disable (works because spawn conditions require interval > 0):
hermes config set skills.creation_nudge_interval 0
hermes config set memory.nudge_interval 0   # if a native memory store is active
```

Verified empirically: after a gateway restart with both keys at 0, no further `thread=bg-review` lines and no further auxiliary-model calls appear in the logs. Manual `/refine` still works.

Related: #26298 (write confirmation for auto-created skills) — complementary; this issue covers cost, visibility, and configurability.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (editable install), Linux x86_64
- Provider: zai; main model glm-5.2 (profiles A/B), auxiliary `background_review` glm-4.5-flash
- Multiple profiles on one host (separate per-profile gateways + direct CLI/cron sessions)

items.title: install.sh --commit with an abbreviated sha silently installs unpinned main and exits 0

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

`install.sh --commit <short-sha>` silently fails to pin: the fetch of the pin target is swallowed by `|| true`, the subsequent `git checkout --detach` then misparses the unknown sha as a pathspec, and the installer still prints success and exits 0. The user ends up on whatever `--depth 1` cloned (latest `main` tip) while believing they are pinned.

## Environment

- Linux (Ubuntu 24.04), fresh install, `curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh -o /tmp/hermes-install.sh`
- `bash /tmp/hermes-install.sh --commit 56e2ba5e --non-interactive`
- install.sh from current main (help text: `--commit SHA   Pin checkout to a specific commit after clone/update`)

## Observed

```
✓ Cloned via HTTPS
fatal: couldn't find remote ref 56e2ba5e
→ Pinning checkout to commit 56e2ba5e...
fatal: git checkout: --detach does not take a path argument '56e2ba5e'
```

…and the script continues; exit code is 0. `git log -1` in `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` shows the latest `main` commit, not the pin.

## Root cause (scripts/install.sh)

1. The clone is `git clone --depth 1 --branch "$BRANCH"` (~line 1370/1375), so an arbitrary commit is never present locally.
2. The pin step (~1395) does:
   ```bash
   if ! git cat-file -e "$INSTALL_COMMIT^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
       git fetch origin "$INSTALL_COMMIT" || true
   fi
   ```
   With an abbreviated sha, `git fetch origin <short-sha>` is refused by the server (`couldn't find remote ref`) — and `|| true` swallows it.
3. `git checkout --detach "$INSTALL_COMMIT"` (~1410) then runs with the object still absent; git resolves the unknown name as a pathspec and dies with the misleading `--detach does not take a path argument` error. The failure is not checked, so the install proceeds and reports success.

A full 40-char sha happens to work on the happy path (GitHub allows full-sha fetches), which hides the bug from anyone testing with full hashes. Short hashes are the natural thing to pass — the help text just says `SHA`.

## Expected

Either of:
- Resolve abbreviated shas before fetching (e.g. `git fetch --depth 1 origin <full-sha>` after expanding via `git ls-remote` isn't possible for shas — so: document/require full 40-char shas and **validate the argument length up front**), and
- **Fail hard**: if the pin target cannot be fetched or checked out, abort with a clear message instead of continuing to a successful-looking unpinned install. A user passing `--commit` is exactly the user who cares which code they run.

## Workaround

```bash
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent
git fetch --depth 1 origin <full-40-char-sha>
git checkout --detach <full-40-char-sha>
VIRTUAL_ENV=$PWD/venv uv sync --locked --extra all --active
```

items.title: [Bug]: xAI max/ultra reasoning aliases clamp to high, not the model's ceiling

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Before submitting
- [x] Searched [existing issues](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues) — closest is #85779 (max/ultra 400 + grok-4.6 allowlist miss). That issue asked for a catalog-driven nearest-neighbor clamp. Current `main` stopped the 400s by hard-coding `max`/`ultra` → `high` and unclamping literal `xhigh` on grok-4.6. The remaining gap is the **alias target**: `max` still does not mean "this model's ceiling".
- [x] Confirmed the clamp is on current `origin/main` (`agent/transports/codex.py` xAI branch + `test_grok_46_clamps_hermes_aliases_to_high`)
- [ ] Ran `hermes debug share` — not needed; this is a deterministic request-builder policy, reproducible from unit tests with no live account

## Bug Description

Hermes `agent.reasoning_effort: max` (and `/reasoning max` / `ultra`) is a **Hermes ladder name**, not an xAI wire value. xAI rejects `max`/`ultra` with `400 Invalid reasoning effort`. That part is fine — those names must be remapped.

The bug is **where they remap**. On every xAI model, including grok-4.6, the Codex/Responses transport maps:

| requested | wire value sent |
|---|---|
| `xhigh` | `xhigh` (passthrough, grok-4.6 family only) |
| `max` | **`high`** |
| `ultra` | **`high`** |

grok-4.6's actual ceiling is `xhigh` (live-verified in #85779 against `api.x.ai /v1/responses`: `minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh` accepted; `max`/`ultra` 400). So a user who configured the strongest Hermes level gets the **second-strongest** xAI level, not the strongest the model can do.

This is the inverse of the monotonic-ladder rule already used elsewhere: a stronger requested level must never resolve weaker than the model's published ceiling.

## Environment

- Hermes version: v0.20.1 (`hermes version`), clamp present on `origin/main`
- OS / platform: Linux; xAI via `xai-oauth` (Responses / `codex_responses`)
- Install type: git
- Python: 3.11

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `agent.reasoning_effort: max` in `config.yaml` (or `/reasoning max`).
2. Use `grok-4.6` with provider `xai` / `xai-oauth`.
3. Inspect the outgoing Responses body (`reasoning.effort`), or run the existing unit test:

```text
tests/agent/transports/test_codex_transport.py::TestCodexTransportXaiReasoningEffort::test_grok_46_clamps_hermes_aliases_to_high
```

4. Observe the wire value is `high`, not `xhigh`.

No live xAI call is required — the test locks the current mapping.

## Expected Behavior

Hermes aliases that are not valid on the provider (`max`, `ultra` on xAI) should clamp to the **highest effort that model actually accepts**:

- grok-4.6 family → `xhigh`
- older Grok (4.5 / 4.3 / …) → `high`
- a future Grok that accepts `max` → `max`

Same "ceiling clamp" other providers already apply:

- LM Studio: `max`/`ultra` → `xhigh` (`agent/lmstudio_reasoning.py`, comment says this "mirrors the ceiling clamp every other provider applies (see agent/transports/codex.py)" — the xAI branch does not)
- Kimi K3: `xhigh`/`max`/`ultra` → `max`
- Codex gpt-5.6: `ultra` → `max` (product tier → wire value)

`xhigh` requested explicitly should keep being sent as `xhigh` on grok-4.6 (already correct).

## Actual Behavior

```python
# agent/transports/codex.py — xAI Responses branch
if not is_grok_46_family(model):
    _effort_clamp["xhigh"] = "high"
_effort_clamp.update({"max": "high", "ultra": "high"})
```

Comment on that block: *"max/ultra remain Hermes aliases for every xAI model."* When grok-4.6 gained `xhigh`, only the **literal** `xhigh` token was unclamped. The aliases stayed pointed at the **historical** xAI ceiling (`high`).

This is locked in as intended current behavior by `test_grok_46_clamps_hermes_aliases_to_high`.

Effect: global `reasoning_effort: max` — the documented "strongest" Hermes setting — silently under-thinks on grok-4.6. Users who want the 4.6 ceiling must know to type `/reasoning xhigh` instead of `max`.

## Root Cause

Partial follow-up to #85779. That issue reported:

- A. grok-4.6 missing from the effort allowlist → effort silently dropped
- B. `max`/`ultra` sent verbatim → HTTP 400

Current `main` addresses B by a static map to `high`, and lets `xhigh` through on the 4.6 family. It did **not** adopt #85779's proposed catalog-driven nearest-neighbor clamp (`clamp_reasoning_effort(effort, allowed)` from models.dev `reasoning_options`). The alias target is therefore the old Grok 4.5 ceiling, not the current model's ceiling.

Likely reason the alias was left at `high`: avoid silently escalating existing `reasoning_effort: max` configs when 4.6 shipped `xhigh`. That is a real compatibility concern, but it makes the Hermes ladder non-monotonic and inconsistent with LM Studio / Kimi / Codex.

## Impact

- Anyone with `agent.reasoning_effort: max` (a common "use the strongest level" config) gets `high` on grok-4.6 and never finds out — no warning, no 400, no `/status` distinction between Hermes name and wire value.
- Switching from a model whose `max` is real (DeepSeek, Codex, Kimi) onto grok-4.6 silently drops a tier.
- Workaround exists (`/reasoning xhigh` / `--reasoning xhigh`) but is undiscoverable unless you read the transport clamp.

## Suggested fix

Prefer the #85779 data-driven path so this does not recur on the next Grok:

1. Clamp Hermes aliases to the model's **published** effort set (models.dev `reasoning_options`, already proposed in #85779).
2. For unknown / missing catalog entries, fall back to a family ceiling (`xhigh` on `is_grok_46_family`, `high` otherwise) — not a hardcoded `high` for every xAI model.
3. Invert `test_grok_46_clamps_hermes_aliases_to_high` to expect `xhigh`; keep `test_older_grok_clamps_xhigh_to_high`.
4. Optional: log a one-line remap (`max → xhigh` for grok-4.6) so `/status` and debug traces show the wire value.

If maintainers want to keep today's no-silent-escalate policy, please document it: `max` on xAI means `high`, forever, and `xhigh` is opt-in. Right now the ladder name implies ceiling and the transport disagrees.

## Related

- #85779 — original grok-4.6 send-path bug (silent drop + max/ultra 400). Proposed the catalog clamp; current `main` only did the static `high` map.
- #62881 — fallback inherited `max` 400s on grok-4.5. Expected normalization there is `max`/`xhigh` → `high` (correct for 4.5). Do not apply that 4.5 ceiling to 4.6.
- #85209 / #85246 — picker should only show levels the model supports.
- #80424 — Grok/xAI parity campaign (bind if still the tracking meta).

items.title: cron lifecycle guard (#30719) false-positives on bash arithmetic division $(( x / y ))

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

`cron/lifecycle_guard.py`'s gateway-lifecycle scanner (issue #30719) produces a false positive on cron scripts containing bash arithmetic division (`$(( x / y ))`), blocking legitimate `hermes cron create` calls with `--no-agent` scripts that have nothing to do with the gateway.

## Reproduction

Any cron script containing a line like:

```bash
echo $(( (a - b) / 86400 ))
```

gets blocked with:

```
Blocked: cron job contains a gateway lifecycle command or persistent
launchctl submit operation. ... (#30719)
```

Minimal repro against the library directly:

```python
from cron.lifecycle_guard import check_gateway_lifecycle, GatewayLifecycleBlocked

SCRIPT = "#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho $(( (100 - 50) / 86400 ))\n"
# write SCRIPT to ~/.hermes/scripts/repro.sh, then:
check_gateway_lifecycle(None, "repro.sh")
# raises GatewayLifecycleBlocked
```

## Root cause

`_iter_command_segments` tokenizes the raw script text with `shlex` using `punctuation_chars=";&|()"`. Bash arithmetic expansion `$(( ... ))` isn't shell-command syntax at all, but the tokenizer doesn't know that — it splits on the `(`/`)` characters inside the arithmetic expression the same way it would for real command grouping. For an expression like `(a - b) / 86400`, the `)` right before `/` closes out the preceding segment, and the *next* segment starts fresh with the bare `/` token (the division operator) as its first element.

`_command_token_index` then treats that isolated `/` as the segment's executable token (nothing precedes it that looks like a `VAR=` assignment to skip past). Since `/` contains a slash, `_iter_referenced_shell_scripts` treats it as a path reference and tries to resolve/read it. `Path("/")` (root) both `is_absolute()` and `.exists()` (it's a real directory), so `_read_referenced_script` hits the `not stat.S_ISREG(...)` branch and returns `(None, unsafe=True)` — which `_contains_unsafe_gateway_action` treats as "fail closed" (`return True`), tripping the same block as an actual gateway-lifecycle command.

So: **any bash arithmetic division inside a cron script's raw text can trip the guard**, regardless of what the script actually does, because the isolated `/` operator resolves to the filesystem root when treated as a path.

## Suggested fix

A couple of options, not mutually exclusive:
- Recognize and skip `$(( ... ))` / `((...))` arithmetic-expansion regions before tokenizing for command segments (mirroring the existing `_SHELL_LINE_CONTINUATION` pre-pass).
- In `_read_referenced_script`, special-case single-character-punctuation "paths" like `/`, `.`, `..` — these are never realistic script references and skipping them removes the "resolves to an existing non-regular file" fail-closed trap without weakening the real protection (script paths worth scanning are never bare punctuation).

## Workaround

Avoid `$(( x / y ))` division syntax in cron scripts; compute the same value via `awk`/`bc` inside a quoted program string instead (arguments to `awk`/`bc` aren't treated as command-shaped by the scanner).

## Impact

Low severity (has a workaround, doesn't allow anything unsafe through), but the failure mode is confusing — the error message talks about gateway lifecycle commands, giving no hint that ordinary arithmetic is the actual cause. Took a fair bit of digging to trace back to the `/` token from an unrelated division operator.

items.title: Desktop: second launch (dock icon or 'hermes desktop') silently kills the running app's backend, breaking connection status
items.body:
## Summary

Launching a **second** Hermes Desktop instance while one is already running (clicking the dock icon, or running `hermes desktop` from a terminal) silently kills the running app's backend process and spawns a replacement. The Electron window survives, but its connection status breaks ("active status" shows broken/disconnected) and any work routed through the old backend is interrupted.

## Environment

- Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME/X11, git checkout at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` (uv-managed venv)
- Hermes desktop packaged app (`apps/desktop/release/linux-unpacked/Hermes`)
- Backend: `python -m hermes_cli.main serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0` (the desktop's headless backend)
- Analysis pinned to commit `eec4d5e` (upstream main as reproduced)

## Repro

1. Launch the desktop app (`hermes desktop`). Note PIDs:
   - Electron main: `.../release/linux-unpacked/Hermes`
   - Backend: `... -m hermes_cli.main serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0`
2. While it runs, launch a second instance — either click the dock icon or run `hermes desktop` in a terminal.
3. Observe: the **old backend PID is gone**, a **new backend boots** (fresh `HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=NNNN` in `~/.hermes/logs/desktop.log`), and the app's connection status is broken even though the window stayed open.

Observed process transition (one run):

```
before: Electron 12839, serve 46728
after:  Electron 12839 (unchanged), serve 49355 (replaced) + new boot in desktop.log
```

In other runs the whole instance was replaced (new Electron + new backend). Either way: a second launch never behaves like the documented "focus the running window".

## Expected behavior (per the code's own intent)

- Single-instance lock, [`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` L14104-L14127](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/eec4d5e/apps/desktop/electron/main.ts#L14104-L14127): a second launch routes **into the running instance** — `if (!_gotSingleInstanceLock) { app.quit() }`, and the lock holder's `second-instance` handler just focuses the window (`ensureMainWindow` → `focusWindow`).
- [`gateway/run.py` L29603-L29615](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/eec4d5e/gateway/run.py#L29603-L29615): a second gateway/backend on the same `HERMES_HOME` **refuses** to start ("Another gateway instance is already running … use 'hermes gateway run --replace' to auto-replace") — replacement is opt-in via `--replace`, never silent.

The observed silent replacement matches neither documented behavior.

## Evidence

### 1. Log excerpt (`~/.hermes/logs/desktop.log`) — SIGTERM followed by fresh boot, twice

```
[2026-08-15T22:01:08.754Z] [hermes] Ignoring stale Hermes backend exit (SIGTERM)
[2026-08-15T22:01:10.848Z] [hermes] [boot] Resolving Hermes backend
[2026-08-15T22:01:12.312Z] [hermes] HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=33259

[2026-08-15T22:08:06.999Z] [hermes] [quick-entry] shortcut CommandOrControl+Shift+Space is already taken by another application
[2026-08-15T22:08:07.321Z] [hermes] Hermes backend exited (SIGTERM)
[2026-08-15T22:08:07.426Z] [hermes] [boot] Resolving Hermes backend
[2026-08-15T22:08:08.888Z] [hermes] HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=39201
```

The second sequence is particularly telling: a second instance's activity (`quick-entry` shortcut already taken → a second instance was up) is followed ~300ms later by `Hermes backend exited (SIGTERM)` and a fresh boot. Across the session the log shows **16** `HERMES_BACKEND_READY` boots.

### 2. `backend-ownership.json` before/after (`~/.config/Hermes/backend-ownership.json`)

- **Before** a second launch: file absent/empty (the running app held no ownership record).
- **After** the replacement: file present, claiming the replacement backend:

```json
{
  "backends": [
    {
      "nonce": "c058de2167ca5bc07d29d8548fba9505",
      "pid": 54440,
      "profile": "default",
      "startMarker": "linux:754664",
      "command": "/home/cwayne/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python -m hermes_cli.main serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0"
    }
  ]
}
```

(`pid` tracked the replacement backend in each observation.)

### 3. Hit rate

**3/3 controlled reproductions** (dock-equivalent `gtk-launch hermes` ×2 and terminal `hermes desktop` ×1) replaced the running backend; two of them replaced the whole instance (Electron included). Combined with the 16 backend boots above, this is deterministic, not a flake.

### 4. Code references (pinned to `eec4d5e`)

- Backend spawn inside `startHermes`: [main.ts L9805](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/eec4d5e/apps/desktop/electron/main.ts#L9805) — reached from `createWindow` → [main.ts L11266-L11273](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/eec4d5e/apps/desktop/electron/main.ts#L11266-L11273), which runs inside `app.whenReady()` (registered at [L14136](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/eec4d5e/apps/desktop/electron/main.ts#L14136)), i.e. **after** the lock check.
- Backend ownership claim: [main.ts L3116-L3124](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/eec4d5e/apps/desktop/electron/main.ts#L3116-L3124); ownership stop path (`process.kill(pid, 'SIGKILL')`): [main.ts L3076-L3091](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/eec4d5e/apps/desktop/electron/main.ts#L3076-L3091); ownership file: [main.ts L702](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/eec4d5e/apps/desktop/electron/main.ts#L702).

## Analysis: the backend spawn is NOT outside the `gotTheLock` guard

I checked whether a second instance can spawn a backend before the lock decision. **It cannot, structurally**: every `spawn()`/`execFile()` call before the lock check at L14107 is a helper process (`cmd.exe start`, `fc-cache`, `git`, `gh`, `curl`) — the backend spawn lives in `startHermes()` (L9805), reachable only through `whenReady`/IPC/update paths that a lock-losing instance never executes (it calls `app.quit()` at L14109 before `whenReady` fires). So there is no "spawn outside the guard" gap to patch directly.

The observable SIGTERM of the old backend immediately after a second instance appears points at a **runtime race in the ownership handoff** (`createBackendOwnership` in `backend-ownership.ts`): a second instance that reaches backend-claim territory (e.g. winning the lock when the first instance's lock/liveness is stale, or claiming ownership before the lock check runs its course) writes `backend-ownership.json`, and the first instance's ownership machinery then stops its own backend (`SIGTERM`→`SIGKILL`, see L3076-L3091 and the SIGTERM teardown comment at L3170). The exact interleaving (which instance wins the lock, and whether the claim/stop path is what sends the SIGTERM) is not yet pinned — I can run an instrumented repro (ownership file + `strace`-level process events across a second launch) if useful.

## Impact

- Clicking a launcher/dock icon while the app is running — a completely normal user action — breaks the running session instead of focusing it.
- Any in-flight agent work routed through the old backend is terminated mid-turn.

## Workaround (local, not a fix)

A focus-or-launch wrapper for the `.desktop` `Exec` that checks for a running Electron main process and just focuses the window, launching `hermes desktop` only when nothing is running. This avoids the second instance entirely.

## Related

- #87269 — separate but adjacent: the generated `.desktop` `Exec` pointed at a Python script with an `env python3` shebang, which crashes under the desktop session's minimal PATH. (Both the fix and its tests are on the PR branch, now re-authored: [c4fbd9a](https://github.com/YappLeCunt/hermes-agent/commit/c4fbd9a), [0215bbf](https://github.com/YappLeCunt/hermes-agent/commit/0215bbf).)

items.title: Windows: ZIP fallback fires on a dependency failure and permanently deletes uncommitted changes + untracked files (no dirty-tree guard)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: python:uv
labels.description: Pull requests that update python:uv code

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Summary

On Windows, a **dependency-install** failure is caught by the same `except subprocess.CalledProcessError` that guards the git update, reported to the user as `⚠ Git update failed`, and escalated to `_update_via_zip()`. The ZIP path then replaces every top-level entry in the checkout except `venv`, `node_modules`, `.git`, and `.env` — with **no dirty-tree guard**. Uncommitted modifications are overwritten and **untracked files are permanently deleted**.

This is strictly more destructive than the `git reset --hard origin/main` path the updater uses elsewhere, which at least leaves untracked files alone. The git pull has *already succeeded* by this point, so the ZIP re-download cannot fix the actual failure (a locked `hermes.exe`) — it only destroys work.

The user still lands on the new commit, so **the failure is silent** unless you inspect the working tree.

### How this differs from the existing reports

- #86093 covers the **trigger** (live `hermes.exe` can't be renamed → `uv pip install -e .` exits 2). Confirmed independently here; not re-litigating it.
- #83846 covers the same escalation but scoped to **build outputs** (`apps/desktop/release/` deleted, never rebuilt). Its fix suggestion is "exclude `apps/*/release/` from the replace".

Neither reports that the ZIP path destroys **source-tree state** — uncommitted edits and untracked files — nor that the fallback is keyed on exception *type* rather than on git actually having failed. Excluding `apps/*/release/` would not fix this.

### Mechanism (all line refs at `fe0a56ed1`, 2026-08-15)

1. `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:4528` opens a ~1900-line `try:` inside `_cmd_update_impl`. It spans the git pull, the auto-stash restore, **and** the dependency install (`→ Updating Python dependencies...`, line 4978).
2. `update_cmd.py:6392` catches `subprocess.CalledProcessError` from *anywhere* in that block. On Windows it prints `⚠ Git update failed: {e}` and calls `_update_via_zip(...)` (6394-6400). On non-Windows it just exits 1, so only Windows takes the destructive path.
3. `_update_via_zip` (776) declares its intended trigger in its own docstring (779): *"Used on Windows when git file I/O is broken (antivirus, NTFS filter drivers ...)"* — i.e. a **git** failure. A `uv pip install` exit 2 is not that.
4. `update_cmd.py:855` — `preserve = {"venv", "node_modules", ".git", ".env"}`. Everything else is replaced.
5. `_commit_staged_replacements` renames the live entry to `<dst>.hermes-update-old`, moves the pristine ZIP copy into place, then at line 755: *"All swaps succeeded — drop the backups"* → `shutil.rmtree(backup)`.

Because step 5 swaps and then deletes at **directory granularity**, every untracked file under a replaced top-level directory is destroyed. There is no `git status --porcelain` / dirty check anywhere in `_update_via_zip`.

### Impact observed

A checkout carrying local modifications lost them on every `hermes.exe update` run, plus untracked directories under replaced top-level entries. The install is additionally left with new Python code but a stale web UI and skipped skill sync, because the post-install stages after the `except` never run.

### Environment

Windows 11 Home 26200, non-elevated pwsh 7, install method `git`, hermes-agent v0.20.1, Python 3.11.15, uv-built relocatable venv.

Supporting measurement for the trigger in #86093 — a warm live shim cannot be renamed, but an ordinary running PE image can:

| binary | size | rename while running (1.5s warm-up) |
|---|---|---|
| `venv\Scripts\hermes.exe` (uv trampoline) | 46080 | **fails** — `0x80070020` ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION |
| `ping.exe` copy (ordinary PE) | 45056 | succeeds |

All the venv shims (`hermes.exe`, `hermes-agent.exe`, `hermes-acp.exe`, `python.exe`) carry a `trampoline` marker. This supports #86093's inference that the launcher holds its own file open without `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`. Note the rename succeeds if attempted immediately after spawn — the warm-up is load-bearing when reproducing.

### Suggested fixes

1. **Scope the fallback to git failures.** A dependency-install failure should not trigger a source re-download — the pull already succeeded. Catch it separately and report it as a dependency failure.
2. **Never let the ZIP path clobber a dirty tree** without explicit opt-in, and don't delete untracked files. At minimum, check `git status --porcelain` and abort with guidance.
3. **Fix the message.** `⚠ Git update failed` when git succeeded sends users hunting in the wrong place.
4. Re-exec the install through `sys.executable` when the shim can't be quarantined (this is #86093's suggestion 3 and would remove the trigger entirely).

Workaround that avoids the whole path, consistent with #86093:

```
venv\Scripts\python.exe -c "from hermes_cli.main import main; main()" update --yes
```

items.title: delegate_task hangs ~600s when target CLI rejects --acp (Claude Code v2.x, others)
items.body:
# Bug: `delegate_task` to Claude Code hangs for full `child_timeout_seconds` when Claude CLI doesn't support `--acp`

## Summary

`delegate_task` with `acp_command: claude` (or `claude` resolved via PATH)
**hangs the parent agent for the full `child_timeout_seconds` (default
600s, observed 109s before user interruption)** whenever the target
Claude CLI version rejects `--acp`. The bug is silent — the parent sees
no output, no error, just a stalled subprocess.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: v0.16.0 (this checkout)
- Claude Code: v2.1.233 (Claude Code at `/home/jacob/.npm-global/bin/claude`)
- Python: 3.14 (host), 3.11 (hermes-agent venv)
- Linux, tmux session
- `delegate_task` invoked from main conversation loop with `acp_command: claude`, `acp_args: [--model, opus, --effort, medium, --max-turns, 1, --max-budget-usd, 0.50]`

## Steps to reproduce

```python
# In a running Hermes session:
delegate_task(
    goal="Reply with one word",
    acp_command="claude",
    acp_args=["--model", "opus", "--effort", "medium",
              "--max-turns", "1", "--max-budget-usd", "0.50"],
)
```

Expected: Either (a) the prompt runs and returns Opus's answer, or
(b) an immediate error explaining that Claude Code doesn't support ACP.

Actual: The `delegate_task` call **stalls with no progress for 109s+
before being interrupted** (or 600s before `child_timeout_seconds`
fires). Tool returns `{"status":"interrupted","duration_seconds":109.0,
"tokens":{"input":0,"output":0}}`.

## Root cause

`tools/delegate_tool.py` → `agent_init.py:746` →
`agent/copilot_acp_client.py:354` builds an ACP client with:

```python
self._acp_args = list(acp_args or args or _resolve_args())
# _resolve_args() default = ["--acp", "--stdio"]
```

The spawned subprocess is:

```
claude --acp --stdio --model opus --effort medium --max-turns 1 --max-budget-usd 0.50
```

`claude v2.1.233` does **not** recognize `--acp`:

```
$ claude --acp --stdio < /dev/null
error: unknown option '--acp'
$ echo $?
1
```

The subprocess exits with code 1 within ~250ms and writes the error to
stderr. The intended fast-fail path in `_run_prompt` (lines ~528–541)
checks `if proc.poll() is not None and stderr_text:` and raises
`RuntimeError(f"Copilot ACP process exited early: {stderr_text}")`.

**However**, in practice the call hangs for many seconds. The most likely
cause is that the stdout reader thread (line 467) and stderr reader
thread (line 476) start with `daemon=True` after `Popen` succeeds, but the
`_request` loop body calls `proc.stdin.write(...)` for `initialize`
**before** the readers have a chance to drain the dying subprocess's
stderr. The reader sees EOF on the pipe, the proc is already dead, but
the deadline check `time.monotonic() < deadline` continues spinning
through `inbox.get(timeout=0.1)` until `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=900`
expires.

The 109s figure observed suggests either the parent's interrupt
mechanism or a downstream wait — either way, the user-visible result is
the same: a silent multi-minute hang with a `tokens: {input:0, output:0}`
result that looks like the child ran but produced nothing.

## Suggested fix (one possible shape)

Probe CLI support before spawning:

```python
def _acp_supported(command: str, args: list[str]) -> bool:
    """Probe whether ``command`` accepts the ACP args we'd pass."""
    try:
        probe = subprocess.run(
            [command, "--help"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
        )
    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError):
        return False
    if probe.returncode != 0:
        return False
    return bool(re.search(r"(?:^|\s)--acp(?:\s|=|\b)", probe.stdout))
```

Then in `CopilotACPClient._run_prompt` (line ~438), **before** the
`Popen` call:

```python
if not _acp_supported(self._acp_command, self._acp_args):
    preview = " ".join(self._acp_args[:3]) if self._acp_args else "(none)"
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"ACP transport not supported by '{self._acp_command}': "
        f"`{preview}` is rejected as an unknown option. This usually "
        f"means the CLI is an older release (e.g. Claude Code v2.x) "
        f"or a different tool than expected. Either install a CLI "
        f"that ships with --acp support (e.g. `@github/copilot` "
        f"late 2025+), or set HERMES_COPILOT_ACP_COMMAND / "
        f"HERMES_COPILOT_ACP_ARGS to a working pair."
    )
```

**Measured:** probe runs in ~50ms; `_run_prompt` now raises in 280ms
instead of hanging for 109s+ (verified locally on the same machine
where the original hang was observed).

## Workarounds

**Option A — bare CLI (recommended for one-off Opus calls):**

```bash
cat > /tmp/prompt.txt <<EOF
<review or strategic prompt here>
EOF
claude -p "$(cat /tmp/prompt.txt)" \
  --model opus --effort medium --max-turns 5 \
  --max-budget-usd 1.00 \
  --add-dir /path/to/project \
  --allowedTools "Read,Bash,Grep"
```

Returns in 9–30s with full output. This is the same recipe that the
bundled `claude-review-delegate` skill documents. Bypasses the broken
ACP transport entirely.

**Option B — `@github/copilot` CLI:**

Install the late-2025+ Copilot CLI which ships with `--acp`:

```bash
npm install -g @github/copilot
export HERMES_COPILOT_ACP_COMMAND=copilot
```

`delegate_task` works correctly when pointed at the new CLI.

## Related context

- The bundled `claude-review-delegate` skill (`software-development/
  claude-review-delegate/SKILL.md`) documents several Opus pitfalls
  (Pitfall 1: `--effort high` no-flush; Pitfall 7: stdin hang) but
  assumes the user calls `claude -p` directly. None of the documented
  pitfalls explain the 109s `delegate_task` stall — this is a separate
  ACP-transport bug, not an Opus model bug.
- Discovered while testing the round-44 PR follow-up: comparing
  language-fluency self-assessments between two models.
- Opus itself is fine — `claude -p "..." --model opus` returns in 4s
  on the same machine. The bug is purely in the `delegate_task` ACP
  path.

## Checklist for the fix

- [ ] Reproduces on `claude v2.1.233` (current)
- [ ] Does NOT reproduce on the new `@github/copilot` CLI (which supports `--acp`)
- [ ] Fast-fail timing on unsupported CLI: <500ms (target: ~280ms as measured locally)
- [ ] No regression on supported CLI: full prompts still complete
- [ ] Error message names the unsupported flag and the expected fix (install new CLI OR set HERMES_COPILOT_ACP_* env vars)
- [ ] Test coverage: unit test that probes `_acp_supported("claude", ["--acp","--stdio"])` returns False without spawning an ACP session

---

**Fix:** #87308 (PR with the patch).

Proposed patch is at https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/87308

items.title: hermes mcp login <server>: OAuth callback port collision makes interactive login impossible on a headless host (v0.20.1) — #5344 regressed

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

On v0.20.1, `hermes mcp login <server>` is **not completable** for an `auth: oauth` MCP server on a headless host. A single invocation emits **two** authorization URLs, then dies binding the callback port it already bound:

```
✗ Authentication failed: OAuth callback port 48407 is already in use ([Errno 98] Address already in use).
  Close any other in-progress login, or set a free `oauth.redirect_port` in the server config, then retry.
```

The failure **tears down the first flow's listener**, so the browser redirect has nothing to hit and the token is never written. Only `mcp-tokens/<server>.client.json` (the DCR registration) is produced.

This looks like #5344 ("MCP OAuth: port collision on concurrent auth + redirect URI mismatch on restart"), which is **closed** — but the code still carries the deferred fix.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent **v0.20.1 (2026.8.13)**, git `165c889e5b`
- Python 3.11.15, OpenAI SDK 2.24.0
- Ubuntu 24.04, headless VPS, no DISPLAY, root, systemd gateway
- Server: hosted streamable-http, `auth: oauth`, dynamic client registration

## Reproduce

```bash
hermes mcp login <oauth-server>
```

## Observed sequence

Line numbers from a single run's output:

```
line  2:  MCP OAuth: authorization required.   <- flow 1: prints URL A, binds port P
line 27:  MCP OAuth: authorization required.   <- flow 2: prints a DIFFERENT URL B
line 50:  Starting OAuth flow for 'recall'...
line 51:  ✗ Authentication failed: OAuth callback port P is already in use
```

Two authorization URLs, one port. After line 51, `ss -tlnp | grep P` shows nothing — the listener is gone, so neither URL can complete.

## Where it comes from

`tools/mcp_oauth.py::_configure_callback_port` documents this itself:

> NOTE: also sets the legacy module-level `_oauth_port` so existing calls to `_wait_for_callback` keep working. **The legacy global is the root cause of issue #5344** (port collision on concurrent OAuth flows); replacing it with a ContextVar is out of scope for this consolidation PR.

Port resolution (`tools/mcp_oauth.py:1095`):

```python
port = requested or _cached_redirect_port(storage) or _reserve_callback_port()
```

Flow 1 reserves/binds `P` and persists it into `<server>.client.json` `redirect_uris`. Flow 2 then resolves `_cached_redirect_port(storage)` — reading `P` straight back out of the file flow 1 just wrote — and re-binds it.

Two independent call sites can each start a flow: `hermes_cli/mcp_config.py:489` and `:813`.

## Ruled out (each still fails)

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| Stop the gateway first (remove the other OAuth consumer) | still fails |
| Pin `oauth.redirect_port: <fixed>` | still fails |
| Leave it unpinned (ephemeral) | still fails |
| Delete `mcp-tokens/<server>.client.json` first | still fails |

So it is **intra-process**, not contention with the running gateway.

## Attempted local patch (reverted — recording what did NOT work)

Screening the resolved port and taking a fresh one when it is unavailable does **not** fix it, because the port actually bound comes from the `_oauth_port` global rather than the return value.

Worth noting for whoever fixes this: a port is unusable in **two** distinct states that need **different** probes —

- **reserved** by `_reserve_callback_port()` — bound but *not listening*, so it refuses `connect()` yet still blocks `bind()`
- **adopted** by a live `HTTPServer` — accepts `connect()`

A `bind()` probe sees only the first; a `connect()` probe only the second. Checking just one reports the process's own reservation as busy and the real listener as free — exactly backwards.

## Impact

On a headless host this makes the OAuth MCP unreachable. The documented remote workarounds both depend on the callback listener surviving:

1. paste the redirect URL at the prompt
2. `ssh -N -L <port>:127.0.0.1:<port> host` and let the redirect complete

Both were tried; the listener is already gone by the time the browser redirects. The tunnel logs `channel N: open failed: connect failed: Connection refused`, and the browser shows `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`.

## Suggested fix

The ContextVar refactor the docstring defers — scope the callback port per flow instead of a module-level global. A narrower fix: have flow 2 detect that a callback server for the resolved port is already live in-process and **await it** rather than binding a second one.

## Workaround for anyone hitting this

Use the server's REST/API path if it has one. In our case the vendor CLI reads the same key and works normally, so only the MCP-only tools are lost.

items.title: install.sh: both install-blocking `npm install` sites run --silent with no output capture, so the failure that now aborts the install is undiagnosable

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### Summary

Since #85537 a failed `npm install` aborts the installer — correctly, that PR fixed a real false-success bug (#77003). But both install-blocking call sites run `npm install --silent` with no output capture, so the failure that now stops the install prints exactly one line and no npm diagnostics:

```
✗ npm install failed or timed out; Node.js dependencies were not installed
```

There is no way to tell EBADENGINE from ETARGET from a network timeout from a registry 5xx. The failure is fatal and silent at the same time.

### Affected call sites

- `scripts/install.sh:2311` — browser tools (`install_node_deps`)
- `scripts/install.sh:2417` — TUI

```bash
if ! run_with_timeout "$NODE_DEPS_TIMEOUT" npm install --silent; then
    log_error "npm install failed or timed out; Node.js dependencies were not installed"
```

### The same file already has the right pattern

The camofox path at `scripts/install.sh:2799-2804` captures and replays npm's output on failure:

```bash
log_file="$(mktemp)"
if ! run_with_timeout "$NODE_DEPS_TIMEOUT" "$npm_bin" install -g ... --silent \
    >"$log_file" 2>&1; then
    log_error "npm install failed or timed out:"
    cat "$log_file" >&2
```

So this is a consistency gap, not a new design — the two sites that can abort an install are the two that don't do it.

### Why this matters now

**Real users are hitting it and cannot report it.** #87093 (Debian 13.6, clean install via `curl | bash`) ends on this exact line. It is labelled `needs-repro`, and the reporter has nothing further to paste, because the installer printed nothing further. That issue cannot progress until this output exists.

**CI has been red on every scheduled run since 2026-08-13 19:40 UTC**, every leg on the same line:

- last green: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/31679596155 (08-13 07:52 UTC)
- first red: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/31737010995 (08-13 19:40 UTC)
- still red: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/31903975622

`npm install` has in fact never succeeded in the install E2E sandbox — #85537 only stopped it from lying about it. The last green run shows the pre-#85537 behaviour verbatim, which is the #77003 pattern:

```
⚠ npm install failed (browser tools may not work)
✓ Node.js dependencies installed
```

### On root cause — deliberately not claiming one

I could not determine why npm fails, and I want to be explicit that the obvious guesses do not survive contact with the evidence:

- Not simply "no network": in the same CI run `uv` resolves 249 packages through the same egress, and #87093 is a real machine whose `apt` and `git clone` both succeeded.
- Not obviously the npm bad-band (`engines.npm` / `engine-strict`, see `npm_supports_npmrc`): the CI legs log `✓ Node.js v22.23.2 found`, meaning that guard passed.

Determining which it actually is requires the output this issue asks for.

### Proposed fix

Mirror the camofox pattern at both sites: redirect to a temp file, `cat` it to stderr on failure. Optionally also tail npm's own `_logs/*-debug-0.log`, which npm writes on every failure and which nothing currently surfaces.

Happy to open a PR if that's welcome.

### Possibly related, not conflated

Both #87093 and every CI leg also emit this immediately before the npm step:

```
Resolving despite existing lockfile due to removal of global exclude newer
error: The lockfile at `uv.lock` needs to be updated, but `--locked` was provided.
⚠ uv.lock sync failed (see uv output above), falling back to PyPI resolve...
```

That one is non-fatal (it falls back and continues), so it is not the failure here — but the hash-verified tier is silently unavailable to everyone, which may deserve its own issue.

items.title: [Bug]: Linear Webhook Signing Secret Custom Logic

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
### Bug Description

The Hermes webhook adapter (gateway/platforms/webhook.py) does not recognize Linear's linear-signature header, so Linear webhook deliveries cannot be authenticated via HMAC. Linear signs the raw request body with HMAC-SHA256 using the webhook signing key and sends the result in the linear-signature header. Because the adapter's _validate_signature() has no branch for that header name, any Linear route with a real secret configured is rejected as "no recognized signature header" — forcing users to run Linear webhooks with INSECURE_NO_AUTH (unauthenticated) or not use Linear webhooks at all.

The algorithm Linear uses is already implemented in the adapter (generic HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, hex-encoded); the gap is purely the missing header-name branch.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a Linear webhook with a signing key (Linear Settings → API → Webhooks).
2. Create a dynamic webhook route in Hermes for Linear, e.g. hermes webhook subscribe linear --secret <key>.
3. Set the same secret on the route (or edit ~/.hermes/webhook_subscriptions.json).
4. Trigger a Linear event (create/update an issue, or post a comment).
5. Observe that the request is rejected with no signature match.

### Expected Behavior

A Linear webhook POST carrying a valid linear-signature header (hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed by the route secret) should be accepted and processed.

### Actual Behavior

The request is rejected. _validate_signature() falls through its GitHub → GitLab → Svix → generic branches and hits the final "no recognized signature header but secret is configured → reject" path, because linear-signature is not among the headers it checks.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Report: https://paste.rs/suQrz
agent.log: https://paste.rs/Pb967
gateway.log: https://paste.rs/ot1z7
gui.log: https://paste.rs/hVxj6
desktop.log: https://dpaste.com/AEHDS62L5
```

### Operating System

macOS 26.5 (Build 25F71)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.19.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

In gateway/platforms/webhook.py, _validate_signature() recognizes these signature schemes only:

- Svix / AgentMail (svix-id / svix-timestamp / svix-signature)
- GitHub (X-Hub-Signature-256)
- GitLab (X-Gitlab-Token)
- Generic V2 (X-Webhook-Signature-V2 + X-Webhook-Timestamp)
- Generic V1 (X-Webhook-Signature)

Linear sends the signature in the linear-signature header instead, which matches none of the above, so the function reaches its terminal return False. No defect in the HMAC logic itself — the verification primitive (hmac.new(secret, body, sha256).hexdigest()) is already correct; the branch for Linear's header name simply doesn't exist.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Add a Linear branch to _validate_signature(), mirroring the existing generic body-only HMAC check but keyed on the linear-signature header:

```
# Linear: linear-signature = <hex HMAC-SHA256 of raw body>
lin_sig = request.headers.get("linear-signature", "")
if lin_sig:
    expected = hmac.new(
        secret.encode(), body, hashlib.sha256
    ).hexdigest()
    return _hmac_str_equal(lin_sig, expected)
```

labels.name: needs-decision

items.body:
## Summary The agent-facing `cronjob` tool's `update` schema omits the `model` and `provider` parameters, even though the handler accepts and applies them. As a result, when the model/provider drift guard tells the agent to pin a cron job via `cronjob action=update job_id= provider=

model=`, the agent cannot actually pass those arguments — they are not in the tool's advertised schema. ## Impact - An agent following the guard's own remediation advice cannot pin the job; the update silently applies only the other supplied fields (e.g. `name`) and reports `success: true`, leaving `model`/`provider` unset and the job still failing closed on its next run. - The remediation path is undiscoverable from the tool's self-description. ## Root cause In `tools/cronjob_tools.py`: - The **handler** applies the values (works correctly): - line 1318: `updates["model"] = _normalize_optional_job_value(model)` - line 1320: `updates["provider"] = _normalize_optional_job_value(provider)` - The **agent-facing schema** (`"parameters"` block, starting line 1463) has **no** `"model"` or `"provider"` keys — verified: `grep -c '"model"'` and `grep -c '"provider"'` over lines 1463–1619 both return `0`. ## The drift-guard message that references the broken path `cron/scheduler.py` (~line 4030) instructs: ``` Skipped to prevent unintended spend: global inference config drifted since this job was created (...), and this job is unpinned. ... To run on the new config, pin it explicitly: `cronjob action=update job_id= provider= model=` (or pin the original values to keep them). See #44585. ``` That command cannot succeed through the agent tool because `model`/`provider` are not in the schema. ## Suggested fix Add `model` and `provider` (and, for consistency, `base_url`) to the `update` action's parameters in the agent-facing schema, matching what the handler already supports. Alternatively, if the omission is intentional, the drift-guard message should not direct the agent to a parameter it cannot set. ## Reproduction 1. Have a cron job created while `model.default = anthropic/claude-opus-5` (so it snapshots that model, `model` unset). 2. Change the global model: `hermes config set model.default moonshotai/kimi-k3`. 3. `hermes config set` warns that the unpinned job will fail closed and suggests `cronjob action=update ... model=`. 4. From the agent tool, call `cronjob(action="update", job_id=..., model="moonshotai/kimi-k3", provider="openrouter")` — the arguments are rejected by schema validation / not forwarded, and the job's `model` remains `None`. ## Environment - hermes-agent @ ed5e17f - Installed via git; single Telegram gateway profile

items.title: Background review drops gateway ephemeral session context and breaks prompt-cache prefix parity

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

labels.name: sweeper:risk-caching
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break/degrade prompt caching or cache-key stability (invariant)

items.body:
## Summary

The background memory/skill review fork does not inherit the parent's `ephemeral_system_prompt`. In Gateway sessions this prompt contains the pinned platform/session context, including the Feishu source and user ID block. As a result, the review request has a different system-prompt prefix from the foreground request and exact prompt-prefix caches (including llama.cpp checkpoint caches) cannot be reused.

## Evidence

A captured foreground prompt contains:

```text
Platform: feishu

## Current Session Context
...
**Source:** Feishu ("DM with <redacted>")
**User ID:** "<redacted>"
...
```

The prompt generated by the automatic background review instead contains:

```text
Platform: feishu<|im_end|>
```

The first divergence is therefore the complete removal of `## Current Session Context`, not an ID rotation. The review harness message is appended afterwards.

## Source of the bug

`gateway/run.py` builds the context prompt into `combined_ephemeral` and passes it as `ephemeral_system_prompt` to the foreground agent. `agent/system_prompt.py` intentionally excludes this field from `_cached_system_prompt`.

`agent/background_review.py` currently copies `_cached_system_prompt` to the fork, but does not copy `ephemeral_system_prompt`:

```python
review_agent._cached_system_prompt = agent._cached_system_prompt
```

Therefore the fork retains the static system prompt but loses the Gateway-injected session context.

## Impact

- Feishu background reviews lose the source/user/session metadata in their effective system prompt.
- The prompt prefix diverges at `Platform: feishu`, causing a full prompt-cache/checkpoint miss instead of reusing the parent's prefix.
- On long contexts this can trigger expensive re-prefill and agent-side timeout/retry symptoms.
- CLI sessions are not affected because they do not receive the Gateway Feishu ephemeral context.

## Proposed fix

Pass the parent's ephemeral prompt when constructing the review fork, without gating it on same-model routing:

```python
ephemeral_system_prompt=getattr(
    agent, "ephemeral_system_prompt", None
),
```

Keep the existing `_cached_system_prompt` inheritance. The effective system prompt requires both pieces, and copying the exact string preserves byte-level prefix parity without moving per-session metadata into the persisted static prompt.

## Regression test

Add coverage asserting that the review fork receives an `ephemeral_system_prompt` byte-for-byte equal to the parent, with a Feishu-style `## Current Session Context` fixture. The existing cache-parity test module is a suitable location.

labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Bug: ACP mode — interrupting a turn with a hung tool call crashes the adapter with `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith'` (JSON-RPC -32603)

### Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13), Windows 11
- ACP mode (`hermes acp`), driven by an ACP host (Paseo daemon v0.4.0)
- Provider: deepseek

### Scenario (observed)
1. Agent starts a turn that runs a terminal tool call which hangs (here: `ls`/`find` under git-bash/MSYS on Windows — known MSYS hang when traversing directories).
2. While the turn is stuck waiting on the tool result, follow-up messages from the user are queued (`Queued for the next turn (N queued)`) and cannot interrupt.
3. The user interrupts the hung tool (SIGINT; the bash subprocess exits with code 130).
4. Instead of recovering cleanly, the ACP turn dies with a JSON-RPC internal error, observed on the host side at the moment of interruption:
   ```
   error: "Internal error: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith'"
   code: -32603
   data: {"details": "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith'"}
   ```

The message format (`'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith'`) is a Python `AttributeError`, so the crash is inside the Hermes ACP adapter, not the host.

### Impact
- The interrupted turn fails instead of resuming/recovering.
- Queued follow-up messages are dropped/blocked by the failed turn state and need a manual interrupt of the whole turn to get the agent back.

### Logging gap (why exact line is unknown)
`acp_adapter/entry.py` (`_setup_logging`) routes all adapter logging **only to stderr**, and the host does not persist the child's stderr, so no traceback is available. Only the JSON-RPC error message reached the host.

Likely spots (`.startswith()` on possibly-`None` values in `acp_adapter/server.py`):
- line 506: `data if data.startswith("data:")` — `data` may be `None`
- lines 1667 / 1690 / 1712: `user_text.startswith(...)` — `user_text` may be `None`
- line 2012: `final_response.startswith(...)` — `final_response` may be `None` on an interrupted/empty turn (most likely, since this fires on interruption)

### Requests
- Guard `.startswith()` calls against `None` in the interrupt/busy paths (fix the crash).
- Log tracebacks for adapter-internal errors (so the exact site is diagnosable).
- Ensure queued messages are flushed or explicitly failed when a turn dies, instead of leaving the session stuck.
