items.title: Classic CLI: Shift+letter prints literal [27;2;<code>~ instead of capital on Ghostty (modifyOtherKeys level 2)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

In the classic interactive CLI, pressing **Shift + letter** (e.g. `Shift+W`)
prints the literal text `[27;2;87~` into the prompt buffer instead of the
capital letter `W`. Same for every Shift+letter/digit/punct combo:
`Shift+H` -> `[27;2;72~`, `Shift+C` -> `[27;2;67~`, etc.

Root cause: the CLI requests xterm **modifyOtherKeys level 2** (`CSI >4;2m`)
from allowlisted terminals, which makes the terminal report *every* modified
key as a `CSI 27;mod;code~` escape sequence. prompt_toolkit (and Hermes'
`pt_input_extras.py`) only decode the Enter/Backspace variants of those
sequences; the Shift+letter sequences fall through the VT100 parser and are
inserted as literal characters.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13), git install
- Python 3.13.12 (conda), prompt_toolkit 3.0.52
- macOS 26.5.2 (Tahoe), Apple Silicon
- Terminal: Ghostty, `TERM=xterm-ghostty`, `TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start the classic CLI: `hermes` in a Ghostty window.
2. Type `Shift+W`.

## Expected vs actual

- Expected: `W` is inserted.
- Actual: `[27;2;87~` is inserted (the `ESC` byte is consumed by the parser
  as the Escape key; the rest lands in the buffer as literal text).

## Root cause

`cli.py`:

- `_EXTENDED_ENTER_KEYS_SEQ = "\x1b[>4;2m"` (level 2) is written to the
  terminal when `_terminal_supports_extended_enter_keys()` matches the
  allowlist (`TERM_PROGRAM in {iTerm.app, WezTerm, ghostty, vscode}`,
  `xterm-ghostty`, kitty, tmux, `WT_SESSION`).
- Level 2 semantics: **all** modified keys are reported as `CSI 27;mod;code~`,
  where `code` is the ASCII value of the resulting (shifted) character.
  `Shift+W` -> `\x1b[27;2;87~`.
- Stock prompt_toolkit 3.0.52 `ANSI_SEQUENCES` only maps the Enter variants:
  `\x1b[27;2;13~`, `\x1b[27;5;13~`, `\x1b[27;6;13~`.
- `hermes_cli/pt_input_extras.py` additionally maps Shift/Ctrl+Enter and
  Cmd+Backspace / Cmd+ForwardDelete (`\x1b[27;9;127~`, `\x1b[3;9~`, ...).
- No mapping exists for `\x1b[27;2;<65..126>~` (Shift+letters/digits/punct),
  so `Vt100Parser` splits the sequence into `Escape` + `[27;2;87~` literal
  characters.

The feature's stated intent is "report Shift+Enter distinctly" — every
sequence Hermes actually decodes has an unmodified form that is a **control
character** (Enter=13, Backspace=127). Level 2 buys nothing over level 1 for
this use case and breaks all Shift+letters.

## Evidence

Minimal parser repro (prompt_toolkit 3.0.52, before any aliases installed):

```python
from prompt_toolkit.input.vt100_parser import Vt100Parser
events = []
p = Vt100Parser(events.append)
p.feed('\x1b[27;2;87~')
print([(e.key, e.data) for e in events])
# [(<Keys.Escape: 'escape'>, '\x1b'), ('[', '['), ('2', '2'), ('7', '7'),
#  (';', ';'), ('2', '2'), (';', ';'), ('8', '8'), ('7', '7'), ('~', '~')]
```

## Proposed fix

`cli.py`: request **level 1** instead of level 2:

```diff
-_EXTENDED_ENTER_KEYS_SEQ = "\x1b[>4;2m"
+_EXTENDED_ENTER_KEYS_SEQ = "\x1b[>4;1m"
```

Level 1 still reports modified keys whose unmodified form is a control
character — `Shift+Enter` (`27;2;13~`), `Ctrl+Enter` (`27;5;13~`),
`Cmd+Backspace` (`27;9;127~`) — exactly the set `pt_input_extras.py`
decodes — while Shift+letters arrive as plain capitals again. All existing
aliases keep working; nothing Hermes maps requires level 2.

## Verification

- `python -m pytest tests/cli/test_cli_shift_enter_newline.py
  tests/cli/test_cli_cmd_backspace.py tests/cli/test_cli_terminal_shortcuts.py
  tests/cli/test_ctrl_enter_newline.py` -> 30 passed, 2 skipped.
- Manual: after restart, `Shift+letter` inserts the capital; `Shift+Enter`
  still inserts a newline.

## Scope

Affects every terminal in the allowlist (`iTerm.app`, WezTerm, ghostty,
vscode, kitty, tmux), not just Ghostty — any of them will emit unmapped
`CSI 27;...~` sequences under level 2. The fix is a one-line constant
change; the whole bug class (unmapped modified-key sequences leaking as
literal text) is resolved for Shift+keys.

items.title: Curator creates recursive _hermes_global directory nesting (13+ levels, 960 WARNINGs per session)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Summary

The Hermes curator creates a `_hermes_global/` subdirectory **inside** the skills directory, then recursively copies the **entire** skills directory (including `_hermes_global` itself) into it. This produces an infinitely recursive nesting:

```
skills/
  _hermes_global/          ← curator-created copy of entire skills/
    _hermes_global/        ← same copy, level 2
      _hermes_global/      ← level 3
        ...                ← 13+ levels deep
```

Each level contains all 92+ skill subdirectories. On Windows, paths exceed `MAX_PATH` (260 chars), so `prompt_builder` fails to parse every nested SKILL.md:

## Error

```
WARNING agent.prompt_builder: Failed to parse skill file C:\Users\xianj\AppData\Local\hermes\skills\_hermes_global\_hermes_global\_hermes_global\...\_hermes_global\creative\p5js\SKILL.md: [Errno 2] No such file or directory
```

**960 WARNING lines per session startup**, ~500 bytes each = ~480KB of log noise per session. The real skill files are duplicated as real directories at every level (not symlinks), consuming ~3.9 GB of disk.

## Environment

```
version: 0.20.0 [win-x64]
os: Windows 10 (BAO-HOME)
python: 3.12.13
profile: default
```

## Root Cause

The curator logic synchronizes global/bundled skills into a `_hermes_global/` subdirectory of the skills root. However, the sync source includes the skills root itself (or `_hermes_global` is inside the sync source), causing it to copy itself into itself recursively.

On the user's machine, `skills/` is a junction pointing to `E:\1_Code\skills-canonical\`. The canonical source contains:
- 92 top-level skill directories (correct)
- `_hermes_global/` — a real directory with 99 items, containing all 92 skills + `_hermes_global/` again
- Recursion depth: 13 levels

## Impact

1. **Log pollution**: 960 WARNING lines per session startup
2. **Disk waste**: 3.9 GB of duplicate skill files (165,978 files)
3. **Startup latency**: prompt_builder attempts to parse 13x92 = ~1,200 non-existent SKILL.md paths
4. **Windows-specific severity**: MAX_PATH (260 chars) makes deeply nested paths inaccessible, masking the real issue as "file not found"

## Use Case

The user keeps many tools/skills installed and expects them to always be available in the background, loaded automatically when needed. The recursive skill directory makes this worse — every session pays the startup cost of scanning 13 levels of duplicates.

## Suggested Fix

The curator should exclude `_hermes_global/` (and any `_*_global/` directory) from its own sync source. The sync target should be a flat directory, not a recursive copy of the entire skills tree.

```python
# In curator sync logic:
sync_source = skills_dir
# Exclude global subdirectories from being copied into themselves
excluded = {"_hermes_global", "_pi_global", "_dormant"}
sync_items = [d for d in sync_source.iterdir() if d.name not in excluded]
```

## Workaround

Delete the `_hermes_global/` directory from the canonical skills source:

```powershell
# Remove junction from skills dir (if junction)
Remove-Item "C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes\skills\_hermes_global" -Force
# Remove real directory from canonical source
Remove-Item "E:\1_Code\skills-canonical\_hermes_global" -Recurse -Force
# Recreate junction to canonical source
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes\skills" -Target "E:\1_Code\skills-canonical"
```

After cleanup: 98 items, 70 valid skills, 0 recursion, 0 WARNINGs.

items.title: Progressive tool loading auto-trigger (tool schema > 10% context) does not fire in 0.20.0

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

PR #6318 introduced progressive tool loading via `tool_search` / `tool_describe` / `tool_call` meta-tools, allowing tool schemas to be loaded on-demand instead of all injected at startup. The PR also described an **automatic trigger**: when tool schemas exceed 10% of context window, the system should switch to compact/progressive mode.

However, in Hermes 0.20.0 the automatic trigger does not fire. With 157 tools (27 built-in + 130 MCP), tool schemas consume ~104K tokens — **52% of a 200K context window** — yet the system loads all schemas in the prompt and never switches to progressive mode.

## Environment

```
version: 0.20.0 [win-x64]
os: Windows 10
python: 3.12.13
profile: default
model: gongyi/deepseek-v4-flash (via custom OpenAI-compatible gateway)
context_length: 200000 (explicitly set in config.yaml)
MCP servers: 15 configured (8 enabled, 7 disabled)
total tools: 157 (before pruning) -> 82 (after manual pruning)
```

## Measured Impact

| Metric | Before pruning | After manual pruning |
|---|---|---|
| Tools | 157 | 82 |
| Tool schema tokens | ~104K | ~57K |
| % of 200K context | 52% | 28.5% |
| Space for conversation | ~96K | ~143K |
| Threshold (10%) | 20K | 20K |

The 52% overhead is 5x the 10% threshold that should have triggered progressive mode.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure 8+ MCP servers with 100+ total tools
2. Set `model.context_length: 200000` in config.yaml
3. Start a new session
4. Observe agent.log: all tool schemas are injected into the system prompt
5. No automatic switch to progressive mode occurs despite 52% overhead

## Use Case

The user keeps many tools installed (MCP servers for GitHub, video analysis, email, calendar, etc.) and expects them to always be available in the background — loaded automatically when needed, without manual enable/disable toggles.

Currently the only workaround is manually disabling MCP servers in config.yaml to reduce tool count. This defeats the purpose of having tools installed: the user must choose between **having tools available** and **having enough context space for conversation**.

Progressive tool loading (when working) would allow all MCP servers to stay enabled while only injecting the schemas the model actually needs per turn — the best of both worlds.

## Expected Behavior

When total tool schema tokens exceed 10% of `context_length`:
1. Automatically switch to progressive mode
2. Replace full tool schemas in system prompt with the compact `tool_search` / `tool_describe` / `tool_call` meta-tools
3. Load individual tool schemas on-demand only when the model calls `tool_search` or `tool_describe`

## Actual Behavior

All 157 tool schemas are injected regardless of size. No automatic switch occurs. The only workaround is manual MCP pruning in config.yaml.

## Workaround

Manual: disable unused MCP servers in `config.yaml` to reduce tool count. Effective but requires the user to know in advance which tools they'll need — not viable for "always available" workflows.

## Related

- PR #6318 — progressive tool loading (merged)
- #10617 — tool schemas occupy 51% of context (open, same root cause)
- #38652 — max_tokens + overhead > context_length (open, related)

items.title: Terminal lifecycle guard false positive: argument text containing a newline + word/word token that resolves to an existing directory blocks innocuous commands (e.g. gh pr create)
items.body:
## Summary

The in-gateway terminal lifecycle guard (`cron/lifecycle_guard.py`) false-positives and blocks a completely innocuous command when an **argument's text contains a `word/word` token right after a newline** and a **directory with that name exists** relative to the command's cwd. The blocked command was a plain `gh pr create`; no gateway lifecycle string appears anywhere in it.

- Version: Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13) — runtime commit `2d45be2488`, Python 3.11.15, WSL2, Discord gateway session (`_HERMES_GATEWAY=1`)
- Also verified the same logic is present on current upstream `main` (`cron/lifecycle_guard.py`, `_read_referenced_script`: `if not stat.S_ISREG(...): return None, True`).

## Reproduction

Run this inside a gateway session, with cwd = any git repo that contains a **directory** named `github` (e.g. a terraform repo with `github/repositories/` stack — any `word/word` path-shaped token whose first segment is an existing directory works):

```sh
cd <repo-containing-a-github-directory> && gh pr create --title "t" --body "## Scope
- github/repositories/ 2 files (not a CI target)"
```

Observed: blocked with

```
Blocked: command or referenced script cannot restart or stop the gateway
from inside the gateway process. ...
```

Minimal trigger shape (the argument text only needs a newline followed by a `word/word` token; quoting does not matter because the guard scans the raw command string):

```sh
gh pr create --title "t" --body "anything
github/repositories/ ..."
```

## Root cause (traced)

Direct regex verdicts are all clean — the block comes from the referenced-script walk:

```python
contains_gateway_lifecycle_command(cmd)                      # False
contains_launchctl_submit_command(cmd)                        # False
contains_gateway_lifecycle_command_or_referenced_script(cmd) # True  <-- even with read_remote_script=None
```

Monkeypatch trace of the walk:

```
SCRIPT CANDIDATE: /home/kkamji/Code/terraform-lab/github
READ: /home/kkamji/Code/terraform-lab/github -> None unsafe= True
```

Chain:

1. `_iter_command_segments` splits the command on control chars, so the multi-line `--body` text becomes its own segment; the token `github/repositories/` (first token of that line) is treated as an **executable/script-path candidate**.
2. `_resolve_terminal_script_path` resolves it against cwd to `<cwd>/github` — which exists, as a **directory**.
3. `_read_referenced_script` opens it, `os.fstat` reports non-regular (`S_ISDIR`), and returns `(None, True)` — the fail-closed branch intended for unreadable files.
4. `unsafe=True` propagates and the terminal tool returns the gateway-lifecycle block.

So the guard conflates "argument text mentions a path-shaped token" with "command executes that script", and then treats "resolved to a directory" as unsafe. A directory cannot be executed or read as a script; this case should be "nothing to scan" like the binary-magic branch, not a block.

## Why this is a real-world trap

Any PR/issue body, commit message, or heredoc that mentions a repo-relative path across a newline (`docs/foo`, `charts/bar`, `github/...`) hits this whenever the first segment matches a real directory in cwd. It cost us three blocked attempts during a routine PR creation; agents naturally conclude the command shape is forbidden and start inventing workarounds.

Related prior reports in the same family (different triggers): #85557 (multi-line `python3 -c` with local DB path), #86010 (path literals in Python cron scripts), #78447 (binary executables). This one is distinct: no script file is involved at all — only argument text plus a same-named directory.

## Suggested fix directions

- In `_iter_referenced_shell_scripts` (or `_resolve_terminal_script_path`), skip candidates that resolve to a directory (a directory can never be the executed script), OR
- In `_read_referenced_script`, return `(None, False)` for `S_ISDIR` (keep `True` for other non-regular types like devices/fifos where opening is genuinely unexpected).

Either keeps the fail-closed posture for genuinely unreadable objects while removing the directory false positive.

## Workaround

Pass long text via `--body-file` (single-line `--body` strings are unaffected), or keep `word/word` tokens on the same line as other text.

items.body:
1|# Bug: `sessions prune` silently skips live-but-idle sessions with no warning
2|
3|## Summary
4|The dashboard "prune" action (and `hermes sessions prune`) only ever deletes
5|**ended** sessions. A session is considered ended when it has a non-null
6|`ended_at` (set by `/exit`, `/clear`, idle-timeout, etc.). Sessions that were
7|abandoned without a formal close — `ended_at IS NULL` — are **never** pruned,
8|regardless of how old or idle they are. The UI gives no feedback that anything
9|was skipped, so to the user it looks like the prune silently failed.
10|
11|## Reproduction
12|1. Have at least one chat session that was simply abandoned (close the tab /
13|   terminal without `/exit`). Its `ended_at` stays NULL.
14|2. Wait until it's older than the chosen prune window (e.g. 1 day).
15|3. Click **Prune** in the dashboard session sidebar, set days = 1, confirm.
16|4. Observe: the old session is **still in the list**. No "skipped" message.
17|
18|Verified on this host: 7 sessions aged 14 days with `ended_at IS NULL`
19|survived `prune --older-than 1`. A raw query confirmed they are the only
20|sessions older than the window, and all 7 are live/unclosed.
21|
22|## Root cause
23|`SessionDB._prune_filter_where` hard-codes `s.ended_at IS NOT NULL`
24|(hermes_state.py:10201), and `prune_sessions` / `archive_sessions` build
25|their WHERE clause through it. There is no path for a *live but idle* session
26|to match, and no count or warning is surfaced about how many candidates were
27|excluded by the `ended_at` guard.
28|
29|## Why the guard exists (don't just delete it)
30|Never pruning a session the user might still be in is a legitimate safety
31|default. The problem is purely that the **skip is invisible**. A live session
32|that hasn't been touched in 14 days is almost certainly abandoned, and the
33|user explicitly asked to clear old stuff.
34|
35|## Suggested fix (minimal, preserves the safety intent)
36|In `cmd_sessions` (hermes_cli/sessions_cmd.py), after computing the
37|`list_prune_candidates` count for prune/archive, also count the sessions that
38|match *every other filter* but fail the `ended_at IS NOT NULL` clause (i.e.
39|live-but-idle within the window). If that count > 0, print a warning before
40|the confirmation prompt, e.g.:
41|
42|```
43|Note: N session(s) older than 1 day were skipped because they are still
44|"open" (never ended). Prune only affects finished sessions. To clear them,
45|use `hermes sessions delete <id>` or archive them first.
46|```
47|
48|Optionally, offer a `--include-live` / "also archive skipped open sessions"
49|flag that routes the skipped set through `archive_sessions` (reversible) so
50|the user can declutter without risking a live conversation.
51|
52|## Impact
53|- Affected surface: dashboard session sidebar "Prune" button + `hermes sessions prune`.
54|- Data risk: none (the guard is over-protective, not under-protective).
55|- UX: looks like a silent failure; erodes trust in the cleanup feature.
56|
57|## Evidence (read-only query used to confirm)
58|```sql
59|SELECT s.id, s.ended_at,
60|       (SELECT MAX(m.timestamp) FROM messages m WHERE m.session_id=s.id) AS last_msg
61|FROM sessions s
62|WHERE COALESCE((SELECT MAX(m.timestamp) FROM messages m WHERE m.session_id=s.id),
63|               s.started_at) < strftime('%s','now','-1 day')
64|  AND s.ended_at IS NULL;   -- 7 rows returned, all 14+ days old
65|```
66|

## Related (found while triaging — not duplicates of the *UX* gap)
- #85680 — sessions never finalize (`ended_at` stays NULL, unbounded leak). Same root
  cause class (NULL-ended sessions), but that issue is about the *leak*; this one is
  about the *prune UI hiding the skip*.
- #85007 — `sessions archive` silently excludes sessions without `end_reason`.
  Same invisible-skip theme on a sibling command.
- #54189, #73848 — broader session-lifecycle / unbounded-growth tracking.

items.title: system prompt timestamp has no timezone or UTC offset — model must guess EST vs EDT

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-caching
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break/degrade prompt caching or cache-key stability (invariant)

items.body:
### What happens

`agent/system_prompt.py` builds the ground-truth date line as a bare date:

```python
timestamp_line = f"Conversation started: {now.strftime('%A, %B %d, %Y')}"
```

producing:

```
Conversation started: Saturday, August 15, 2026
```

The model is told *what day it is* but not *what zone it is in*.

### Why that matters

Tools that accept instants reject naive datetimes and require an explicit UTC offset. A representative MCP contract:

> Send a timezone-aware ISO-8601 datetime with an explicit offset or `Z` (e.g. `2026-06-20T12:30:00-04:00`). Naive datetimes are REJECTED.

With only a date, the model has to infer the offset itself. For most of the year it guesses right from the month. Near a DST transition it is a coin flip, and a wrong guess does not error — it silently writes the record onto the wrong day or hour.

`hermes_time` already resolves the zone correctly (`get_timezone()`); the value simply never reaches the prompt.

### Related

- #86938 — timestamp goes stale after UTC midnight. Orthogonal: that issue is about *refreshing* the line, this one is about *what the line contains*.
- #84075 — agent uses conversation-start time rather than OS clock.

items.title: ACP mode slash commands don't cover skills and host can't render agent slash list

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Best-effort: we will get to it when we get to it (no commitment)

items.body:
## Bug/Feature: ACP mode slash commands don't cover skills (`/skill` etc.), and the host UI can't render the agent's slash list

### Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13), Windows 11
- ACP mode (`hermes acp`), host = Paseo daemon v0.4.0

### Problem
In ACP mode:

1. Typing `/` in the host's input box shows the **host's own** slash menu — the agent's commands/skills are never rendered. (This part is inherent to ACP host/agent split unless a capability for listing commands is added.)
2. Even when the user types a full slash command, the ACP adapter only dispatches a **curated 9-command subset** — `acp_adapter/server.py` `_handle_slash_command` registry:
   ```
   /help  /model  /tools  /context  /reset  /compress  /steer  /queue  /version
   ```
   There is **no skill dispatch** (`/skill`, skill invocation). Any other `/...` input falls through to the LLM as plain prose (per the code comment: "unrecognized commands fall through to the LLM").

Meanwhile the `hermes-acp` toolset *does* include skills as tools (`skill_view`, `skill_manage`, …), so skills are usable but only via the tool path — users who are used to `/skill` style interaction lose that in ACP mode.

### Expected
- ACP-mode slash dispatch should cover skills (at minimum `/skill` and friends), so a user can invoke a skill the same way they would in the TUI/CLI.
- Ideally, expose the available slash commands to the host so the input box can render/autocomplete them (if the ACP protocol/agent capabilities allow — e.g. via `configOptions` or an extension).

### Notes
- This also affects discoverability: without the `/` menu and with no `/help` overlap for skills, ACP-hosted users have no way to learn which skills exist other than reading the toolset.

items.title: [Feature]: Let desktop plugins see when the focused chat is working
items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Desktop plugins can already read the focused session, the model, and the gateway socket. They cannot read whether the focused chat is in a live turn.

After the user sends a message, a plugin has no simple flag for "the model is working." That covers the wait for the first token and the stream that follows. A plugin that wants to react (a status chip, an avatar pose, a live badge) has to guess from raw gateway events.

### Proposed Solution

Add two readonly atoms on `host.state`:

- `busy`: true while the focused chat is working after a send
- `awaitingResponse`: true from send until the first assistant output

These should follow the same session slice the chat pane already uses. A new draft with no runtime id should fall back to the global flags. A background chat should not leak into the focused flags.

Plugins subscribe with `useValue(host.state.busy)`. Old plugins keep working. They just ignore the new keys.

### Alternatives Considered

A plugin can listen to `message.start`, `message.delta`, and `message.complete` and rebuild this itself. That is easy to get wrong when the user switches chats mid turn. A first class flag is the same source the chat pane already trusts.

A new gateway event such as `thinking.start` is not needed. The chat already has this state.

### Feature Type

Other

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

### Contribution

- [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

items.title: Windows: `hermes update` spawned from the gateway's own /update command can't pause the gateway — ancestor-exclusion in `_scan_gateway_pids` excludes the gateway itself

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
---
title: "Windows: `hermes update` spawned from the gateway's own /update command can't pause the gateway — ancestor-exclusion in `_scan_gateway_pids` excludes the gateway itself"
labels: [bug, windows, gateway]
---

## Summary

On Windows, running `/update` from a messaging platform (Telegram etc.) makes the updater report:

```
✗ Other Hermes processes are running from this install's venv:
  PID 14112  python.exe ... gateway run  ← gateway
  On Windows these keep native extension files (.pyd) locked...
```

The update refuses to proceed and tells the user to close the gateway — but the gateway is the very process that spawned the update, and the pause machinery never finds it.

## Root cause

`hermes update --gateway` is spawned **by the gateway itself** when `/update` is issued from a messaging platform (`gateway/slash_commands.py` → `subprocess.Popen([... "update", "--gateway"], ..., **windows_detach_popen_kwargs())`).

Inside the updater, `hermes_cli/gateway.py:_scan_gateway_pids()` starts with:

```python
# Exclude the entire ancestor chain so the CLI process that invoked this
# scan (e.g. ``hermes gateway status``) is never mistaken for a running
# gateway.  See #13242.
exclude_pids = exclude_pids | _get_ancestor_pids()
```

`_get_ancestor_pids()` walks the current process's parent chain up to PID 1. When the updater is a child of the gateway (the `/update` path), **the gateway's own PID is in that ancestor chain**, so:

1. `_pause_windows_gateways_for_update()` → `find_gateway_pids(all_profiles=True)` returns `[]` — the gateway is excluded as an "ancestor"
2. The updater believes no gateway is running and skips the pause
3. The update proceeds to mutate the venv while the gateway (still alive, still holding `.pyd` files) locks it
4. The venv-holder guard then fires the "Other Hermes processes are running from this install's venv" error and aborts

## Repro evidence (Windows 11, v0.20.1)

With two gateway processes alive (`5264` venv launcher + `22680` uv worker), both with cmdline `... -m hermes_cli.main gateway run --replace`:

```python
>>> from hermes_cli.gateway import find_gateway_pids, find_profile_gateway_processes
>>> list(find_gateway_pids(all_profiles=True))
[]                                  # ← gateway excluded as "ancestor"
>>> list(find_profile_gateway_processes())
[(22680, 'default')]                # ← PID-file path still sees it
```

Manual scan with the same matchers (wmic output + `looks_like_gateway_runtime_command_line` + profile match) finds **both** processes correctly; the only thing removing them is `_get_ancestor_pids()`:

```
_get_ancestor_pids() 返回: {..., 5264, ..., 22680, ...}
```

Also confirmed: both processes pass `_is_pausable_gateway()` (`gateway run` cmdline), so the pause machinery *would* handle them if discovery hadn't excluded them.

## Expected behavior

`hermes update` spawned by the gateway should be able to pause (and later resume/restart) the gateway that spawned it — the ancestor exclusion in `_scan_gateway_pids` is meant to avoid false-matching a `hermes gateway status` CLI, not to hide a real running gateway from the update pause machinery.

## Suggested fix directions

- In the update pause path, don't exclude the gateway that spawned the update — e.g. seed the ancestor exclusion with `exclude_pids` **before** spawning the detached updater (pass the gateway PID explicitly), or
- Have `_pause_windows_gateways_for_update` use the PID-file/profile-based discovery (`find_profile_gateway_processes`) as an additional source instead of relying solely on `find_gateway_pids`, or
- When the update was spawned with `--gateway` (i.e. by the gateway itself), explicitly exclude only the *calling* CLI process rather than the whole ancestor chain.

## Workaround (current)

Run `hermes update` from a standalone terminal (not from the gateway's `/update`), or stop the gateway first. `--force-venv` bypasses the guard but risks a half-updated install.

items.title: gateway: cron scheduler permanently stalls after EMFILE while heartbeat keeps reporting healthy

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-automation
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect CI, automerge, label sync, or maintainer automation

items.body:
## Symptom

After a cron job execution hit `OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files` (likely via the known FD-leak family: #60859, #79742, #80792), the gateway process **survived but its cron scheduler never ran another job** — while the gateway heartbeat file kept updating on schedule, so every external health check reported the profile healthy.

Observed timeline (macOS 15.x / Darwin 25.3.0, launchd-managed gateway, Slack platform):

- Day 1 ~21:07 — a scheduled job's session ends with `Too many open files` blocking all subprocess and filesystem work; `cron/jobs.json` records `last_error: "Failed to read cron database: [Errno 24] Too many open files"`.
- Day 1 21:07 → Day 2 ~20:45 (≈24h) — **zero cron sessions execute** despite a `*/15`-style schedule with `enabled: true` and past-due `next_run_at`. Two independent jobs in the profile were both stalled.
- Throughout: `state/gateway.heartbeat` mtime stayed current (minutes-fresh) and `gateway_state.json` reported `"gateway_state": "running"`, `platforms.slack.state: "connected"`.
- `hermes gateway restart` fully recovered scheduling immediately (drain timed out at 0s; launchd force-restart).

## Why this is its own bug

The FD leaks have their own issues; this one is about **failure containment**: EMFILE in the ticker/executor path leaves the scheduler in a dead state that (a) is not retried/recovered once FDs would free, and (b) is invisible to the liveness surface — the heartbeat keeps beating, so supervision (launchd watchdogs, external monitors keyed on heartbeat/gateway_state) never intervenes. A 24-hour silent scheduling outage on a "healthy" gateway.

## Expected

Either self-recovery (scheduler tick survives EMFILE and retries after backoff), or the failure escalates into the health plane: heartbeat stops / `gateway_state` degrades / systemd-watchdog-equivalent on macOS fires, so a supervisor can restart the process.

## Diagnostics available

- `cron/jobs.json` snapshot with the stalled `next_run_at` and `last_error` (EMFILE reading the cron DB).
- Session store showing the ≈24h gap in `source='cron'` sessions against a 15-minute schedule.
- `gateway_state.json` + heartbeat mtimes during the stall (both healthy-looking).
- Happy to attach lsof-style FD counts on next occurrence; the process was restarted before capture this time.

items.body: ### Bug Description ## Bug Description Hermes Desktop reads every assistant response aloud twice when "Read responses aloud" is enabled. The Desktop UI footer shows: - client v0.20.1 (+2) - backend v0.20.1 However, for one assistant reply the client opens two separate `/api/audio/speak-stream` WebSockets. ## Environment - OS: Windows - Hermes Desktop client: v0.20.1 (+2) - Hermes backend: v0.20.1 - Remote gateway URL: hermes-agent-nmqe.srv1899170.hstgr.cloud - TTS provider: edge - Edge voice: de-DE-AmalaNeural - Desktop "Read responses aloud": enabled Backend/platform voice mode for Desktop is already disabled: ```json { "telegram:8852724051": "all", "desktop:None": "off", "desktop:": "off" } ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open Hermes Desktop v0.20.1 on Windows. 2. Connect to a remote Hermes backend v0.20.1. 3. Enable "Read responses aloud". 4. Open DevTools Console. 5. Patch WebSocket constructor to log /api/audio/speak-stream opens. 6. Send a short message, e.g. test. 7. Observe two separate /api/audio/speak-stream WebSockets for the same assistant reply. ### Expected Behavior Only one /api/audio/speak-stream session should be opened per assistant message. The assistant response should be spoken once. ### Actual Behavior For one assistant reply, Desktop opens two separate speak-stream WebSockets: 2026-08-16T11:07:33.393Z wss://.../api/audio/speak-stream?...&profile=default 2026-08-16T11:07:37.558Z wss://.../api/audio/speak-stream?...&profile=default Both WebSockets are opened from the same JS bundle location: new WrappedWebSocket .../app.asar/dist/assets/index-CJ6IrMK4.js:208:3729 Server logs confirm two independent TTS generations for one assistant turn: text 2026-08-16 11:07:28 agent.turn_context msg='test' 2026-08-16 11:07:31 Turn ended 2026-08-16 11:07:31 tools.tts_tool: Generating speech with Edge TTS... 2026-08-16 11:07:32 TTS audio saved 2026-08-16 11:07:35 tools.tts_tool: Generating speech with Edge TTS... 2026-08-16 11:07:35 TTS audio saved dashboard-auth.log also shows two speak-stream ticket mint events for the same reply: 2026-08-16T11:07:31.325884+00:00 ws_ticket_minted 2026-08-16T11:07:35.501558+00:00 ws_ticket_minted ### Affected Component CLI (interactive chat) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) _No response_ ### Debug Report ```shell Report https://paste.rs/DXqUU agent.log https://paste.rs/dopxW gateway.log https://paste.rs/ymi2y gui.log https://paste.rs/ntIJw ``` ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Python Version _No response_ ### Hermes Version _No response_ ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell The WebSocket request User-Agent still contains: Hermes/0.17.0 but the Desktop UI footer shows: client v0.20.1 (+2) backend v0.20.1 So the Hermes/0.17.0 User-Agent may be a separate packaging/version metadata bug, not necessarily the cause of this issue. ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) The same Desktop read-aloud handler appears to be invoked twice for the same assistant message. Because both WebSockets originate from the same bundle location: index-CJ6IrMK4.js:208:3729 this looks like a client-side idempotency issue, possibly: - one trigger on final assistant message, - another trigger on message/history/state replay, - duplicate React effect/listener registration, - or the same assistant message being processed twice by the read-aloud pipeline. ## Suggested Fix Make Desktop read-aloud idempotent per assistant message. For example, track started/completed read-aloud sessions keyed by: - `message.id` if available, - otherwise `sessionId + normalized assistant text hash`. Ignore duplicate speak-stream starts while a speech session for the same assistant message is already active or recently completed. ### Proposed Fix (optional) ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

### What's Going Wrong?

Following the official Termux install path (`curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash`), the install stalls indefinitely at the `cryptography` build step. `pyproject.toml` currently pins `cryptography==50.0.0` (recently bumped from `48.0.1` for CVE-2026-69247 / GHSA-m2h6-j472-rp4c / GHSA-jwv3-5hgf-82ww). items.title: [Bug] Aux vision client cache poisoned by probe-mode stub — sync vision calls fail with '_AuxProbeClientStub used as a real client'

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

`_get_cached_client()` in `agent/auxiliary_client.py` writes a probe-mode `_AuxProbeClientStub` into the module-level `_client_cache` on a cache miss, because the store site lacks the `isinstance(client, _AuxProbeClientStub)` guard that `_store_cached_client()` has. Since the first client resolution in any fresh process happens inside `aux_probe_mode()` (tool-gating `check_vision_requirements()`), the stub is cached at session start and every subsequent **sync-path** runtime vision call (e.g. `browser_vision` via `call_llm(task="vision")`) receives the dead stub and fails with:

```
_AuxProbeClientStub used as a real client (attribute 'chat'); aux_probe_mode is for availability checks only
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13) — also present in current `main`
- Repro'd on Linux (container), gateway profile; mechanism is process-lifetime so it affects CLI sessions too (check_fn runs at session start there as well)

## Root cause

Design invariant stated at `_AuxProbeClientStub` (agent/auxiliary_client.py):

> "Stubs are never cached (see `_store_cached_client`), so runtime callers can never receive one."

`_store_cached_client()` honors this (guard at ~line 7410), but `_get_cached_client()` — the wrapper used by *every* resolution path (`resolve_vision_provider_client`, `call_llm`, retry paths) — does **not**. On a cache miss it builds the client via `resolve_provider_client()` and writes it directly:

```python
# _get_cached_client(), installed v0.20.1 ~line 7685 / main ~line 7805
if client is not None:
    bound_loop = current_loop
    with _client_cache_lock:
        if cache_key not in _client_cache:
            while len(_client_cache) >= _CLIENT_CACHE_MAX_SIZE:
                evict_key = next(iter(_client_cache))
                del _client_cache[evict_key]
            _client_cache[cache_key] = (client, default_model, bound_loop)
        else:
            built_client = client
            client, default_model, _ = _client_cache[cache_key]
            _close_cached_client(built_client)
```

Inside `aux_probe_mode()`, `_create_openai_client()` returns `_AuxProbeClientStub(api_key=..., base_url=...)` — which is not `None`, so it gets cached. The cache key does not distinguish probe from runtime resolution, so the next real call is a cache hit on the stub.

## Deterministic reproduction

```python
from agent.auxiliary_client import aux_probe_mode, resolve_vision_provider_client, _AuxProbeClientStub

# 1) what check_vision_requirements() does at session start (cold cache)
with aux_probe_mode():
    _, c1, _ = resolve_vision_provider_client()
print(type(c1).__name__)          # _AuxProbeClientStub  (now cached)

# 2) what call_llm(task="vision") does at runtime
_, c2, _ = resolve_vision_provider_client()
print(type(c2).__name__)          # _AuxProbeClientStub  -> RuntimeError on .chat
print(isinstance(c2, _AuxProbeClientStub))  # True

# 3) healing: evict the poisoned entry
_evict_cached_clients("<provider>")
_, c3, _ = resolve_vision_provider_client()
print(type(c3).__name__)          # OpenAI  (real client)
```

Observed with `auxiliary.vision.provider: opencode-go` / `model: minimax-m3`; any provider whose vision resolution goes through `_get_cached_client` is affected.

## Proposed fix (reviewed by two independent reviewers + empirically verified)

Use a **probe-backed predicate** (unwraps adapter wrappers) at **all three cache sites** — the plain `isinstance` guard is insufficient because `CodexAuxiliaryClient` / `AnthropicAuxiliaryClient` wrap the `_create_openai_client()` result, and in probe mode that inner client is a stub; the wrapper is constructible (the stub's `api_key`/`base_url` slots satisfy the adapter's reads) and is **not** an `_AuxProbeClientStub`, so it sails past `isinstance` guards (verified: wrapper constructed around stub, `isinstance` False). The same gap exists in the existing `_store_cached_client` guard.

```python
def _is_probe_backed_client(client: Any) -> bool:
    if isinstance(client, _AuxProbeClientStub):
        return True
    return isinstance(getattr(client, "_real_client", None), _AuxProbeClientStub)
```

1. **Write side** — don't cache probe-backed clients:
   ```python
   if client is not None and not _is_probe_backed_client(client):
   ```
2. **Read side** — heal already-poisoned caches (protects long-lived processes started before the fix):
   ```python
   if _is_probe_backed_client(cached_client):
       del _client_cache[cache_key]   # evict; fall through to build a real client
   elif async_mode:
   ```
3. **`_store_cached_client`** — replace its `isinstance` guard with the predicate (same wrapped-stub gap).

## Suggested regression tests

- Probe-mode resolution must leave `_client_cache` **empty** (not merely stub-free).
- Cold probe → runtime sequence (same sync key) returns a real, usable client (`.chat` works).
- A preseeded poisoned entry (bare stub *and* a wrapped stub via `CodexAuxiliaryClient`) is evicted on read and replaced.
- **Parametrize the wrapped-stub tests over every adapter class** (Codex, Anthropic, xAI) — enforces the `_real_client` contract by test, not by convention (reviewer: Kimi K3).
- **False-positive test**: an adapter wrapping a REAL client must cache, hit, and serve normally — the regression the predicate is most likely to introduce.
- Same-loop async hit: a wrapped-stub entry is evicted for async callers too (covers the `elif async_mode` restructure).
- No probe-backed client remains cached after any of the above.

Note: with both write sites guarded, the read-side evict only fires for preseeded/directly-mutated caches — it is defense-in-depth/healing; the code comment should say so to prevent future "dead code" removal. Known soft spot: the predicate hard-codes the `_real_client` attribute convention (a future adapter exposing the inner client under a different name would slip through); a bounded recursive check or an assert of single-level wrapping would close that.

## Notes

- `_store_cached_client()` and `_refresh_nous_auxiliary_client()` already guard stubs; `_get_cached_client()`'s direct write (~line 7700 in v0.20.1, ~line 7819 in `main`) is the only unguarded cache write.
- **Scope refinement (verified empirically):** the cache key includes `async_mode`, so the poisoned entry only affects **sync-path** callers. `async_call_llm` consumers (e.g. `vision_analyze`) build their own real client under a different key and work fine — confirmed: `vision_analyze` succeeds while `browser_vision` fails in the same process. Every **sync** `call_llm(task=...)` caller whose first resolution happens in probe mode (tool gating) is affected.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop local pack inherits CI=1 and triggers Electron Builder publishing

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Bug Description

`hermes desktop` on current `main` fails while building the normal local unpacked Desktop app. The Desktop launcher now passes `CI=1` to `npm run pack`; Electron Builder 26.15.3 interprets that as an implicit publishing request and then aborts while resolving publish metadata from `apps/desktop`.

This appears to be a regression introduced by #87440 / merge commit `7f1c49cda`, which routed the Desktop build through `_npm_lifecycle_env()` to scrub `ESBUILD_BINARY_PATH`. That helper also always sets `CI=1`.

I searched open and closed issues/PRs for the two exact error messages and for Desktop + Electron Builder + CI; I did not find an existing report for this regression.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Update a git installation to current `main` at `7095e23eb2066fe9a2f93b99cdbfe0e2b5ece397`.
2. Run:

   ```bash
   hermes desktop --force-build --build-only
   ```

3. The dependency install and Vite build complete, but Electron Builder fails during local `--dir` packaging.

## Expected Behavior

`hermes desktop` should create the local unpacked Desktop artifact without entering any publishing path.

## Actual Behavior

Electron Builder reports:

```text
• electron-builder  version=26.15.3 os=7.1.8-1-cachyos
• Implicit publishing triggered by CI detection. This behavior will be disabled in electron-builder v27. Please use --publish explicitly.
...
⨯ Cannot detect repository by .git/config. Please specify "repository" in the package.json
...
✗ Desktop GUI build failed
```

The checkout is a valid Git repository and the root `package.json` has repository metadata. The failure occurs because publishing was entered unintentionally; `apps/desktop/package.json` itself has no `repository` field.

## Affected Component

Setup / Installation; Desktop launcher (`hermes_cli/main.py`) and Electron packaging.

## Environment

- OS: CachyOS Linux, kernel `7.1.8-1-cachyos`
- Hermes: `v0.20.1 (2026.8.13)`
- Commit: `7095e23eb2066fe9a2f93b99cdbfe0e2b5ece397`
- Python: `3.11.15`
- Node: `v24.19.0`
- npm: `11.17.0`
- Electron Builder: `26.15.3`
- Install method: user-local Git checkout

No debug bundle was uploaded because the exact build failure, differential probe, and relevant environment are included here without uploading unrelated config or logs.

## Root Cause Analysis

Before #87440, the Desktop pack subprocess used the ordinary Desktop environment. After #87440, `cmd_gui()` does:

```python
npm_build_env = _npm_lifecycle_env(env)
build_result = subprocess.run(
    [npm, "run", build_script], cwd=desktop_dir, env=npm_build_env, check=False
)
```

`_npm_lifecycle_env()` currently constructs:

```python
run_env = {**os.environ, **(env or {}), "CI": "1"}
```

Electron Builder's `PublishManager` sees `ci-info.isCI` and changes the implicit publish policy to `onTagOrDraft`. That causes publish metadata resolution during an ordinary local `--dir` build and produces the fatal repository error.

Differential confirmation:

- `hermes desktop --force-build --build-only` fails with implicit CI publishing.
- Running the same builder without the synthetic CI variable succeeds:

  ```bash
  cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop
  env -u CI npm run builder -- --dir
  ```

## Verified Local Workaround

Removing only the synthetic `CI` variable from the packaged Desktop build environment before `npm run pack` fixes the failure:

```python
npm_build_env = _npm_lifecycle_env(env)
if not source_mode:
    npm_build_env.pop("CI", None)
```

Verification after that change:

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gui_command.py`: `26 passed, 5 skipped`
- `hermes desktop --force-build --build-only`: successful packaged artifact
- A second `hermes desktop --build-only`: content stamp matched and the artifact was accepted

## Proposed Fix

Keep the `ESBUILD_BINARY_PATH` scrubbing from #87440, but ensure local Desktop packaging is explicitly non-publishing. Two narrow options:

1. Pass Electron Builder `--publish never` for the local `pack` / `--dir` path, preserving `CI=1` for npm lifecycle behavior; or
2. Remove the synthetic `CI` variable only from packaged Desktop builds, as in the verified workaround above.

A regression test should assert that `hermes desktop --build-only` cannot enter Electron Builder's implicit publishing path merely because Hermes synthesized `CI=1`.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

I can submit the tested narrow fix if maintainers confirm which of the two approaches they prefer.

items.title: [Feature] Proposal: per-tool in-context persistence thresholds + durable artifact pointers (ingress elision)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
---
title: "[Feature] Proposal: per-tool in-context persistence thresholds + durable artifact pointers (ingress elision)"
labels: ["enhancement"]
---

## Summary

Tool results stay fully in context up to a fixed persist threshold (default 100k chars), then old results are pruned to an **unrecoverable** placeholder `[Old tool output cleared to save context space]`. This proposal adds:

1. A config surface `tools.budget.tool_overrides` — per-tool max in-context chars for tool results.
2. A durable artifact directory (configurable, survives restarts — today it's a temp dir).
3. A **recoverable** prune placeholder: one-line summary + absolute pointer, retrievable via `read_file offset/limit` (no LLM involved in elision).

## Why it matters

Long agent sessions are dominated by tool-result tokens being re-sent every turn. In a 48h window on a real install, the two largest sessions processed ~122M / ~107M tokens (~95% cache re-reads), with 72–97% of message content from tool results and 30–60 results >3k tokens per session.

A/B on a scripted 20-step workload (deepseek-v4-flash, off-peak): persisting results >~3k tokens to files with pointers cut **input tokens 92%, processed tokens 37%, estimated cost 76%**, with equal answer quality (5/5 exact strings).

Additional observed failure: when the harness collapses oversized results, the agent re-runs tools to recover exact content, re-paying full payloads as input misses. A recoverable artifact pointer eliminates the whole re-run pattern at ingress.

## Proposed behavior

1. `tools.budget.tool_overrides`: per-tool persist thresholds via config (default unchanged: 100k chars).
2. Durable artifact dir, configurable, survives restarts.
3. Placeholder = one-line summary + absolute pointer, recoverable via `read_file offset/limit` (no LLM in elision).
4. Tool-side caps on terminal/search output remain.

## Open questions

- Default threshold value (8–12k chars proven live; window-scaled default currently 100k).
- Interaction with the existing display-budget collapse path.
- Peak-rate economics (off-peak cache-hit pricing is 1/31 of miss; the win is input-miss elimination, not cache reduction).
- Whether persisted artifacts need TTL / cleanup policy.

## Environment

- Hermes 0.20.1 (v2026.8.13), Linux VPS, gateway (Telegram + desktop)
- deepseek-v4-flash provider, off-peak rates 2026-08-16

items.title: [Desktop] "Read Aloud Replies" triggers TTS synthesis and playback twice per message due to temporary-to-canonical ID mutation

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Bug Description

When **Read Aloud Replies** (`autoSpeak`) is enabled in the Hermes Desktop App, a single assistant response causes **two separate backend TTS synthesis requests** and plays the audio twice back-to-back.

### Root Cause Analysis

1. **First Synthesis & Playback (Streaming Finish)**:
   - When an assistant turn finishes streaming, `useAutoSpeakReplies` detects the message in `$messages`.
   - At this stage, the message carries a temporary client-side streaming ID (e.g., `msg-temp-123`).
   - `speakLatest()` triggers `playSpeechText()`, calling the backend TTS API (e.g., `/api/audio/speak`), and sets `lastSpokenIdRef.current = 'msg-temp-123'`.
   - The first audio starts playing, setting `$voicePlayback.status = 'speaking'`.

2. **ID Mutation During Playback**:
   - While the first audio is playing, the backend finalizes the turn and persists the message into SQLite (`state.db`).
   - The message ID in `$messages` is updated to its canonical database ID (e.g., `msg-db-456`).
   - While playing, `useAutoSpeakReplies` guards against re-triggering because `$voicePlayback.status !== 'idle'`.

3. **Second Synthesis & Playback (Playback Ended)**:
   - When the first audio finishes playing, `$voicePlayback.status` transitions from `'speaking'` to `'idle'`.
   - The subscriber `$voicePlayback.listen(speakLatest)` fires `speakLatest()`.
   - `pendingReply()` compares `last.id` (`msg-db-456`) against `lastSpokenIdRef.current` (`msg-temp-123`).
   - Because `msg-db-456 !== msg-temp-123`, `pendingReply()` incorrectly identifies the message as an unspoken reply.
   - A **second TTS API call** is dispatched to the backend, causing the audio to synthesize and play a second time.

### Affected Files

- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-auto-speak-replies.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-voice.ts` (`pendingResponse` / `consumePendingResponse`)

### Suggested Fix

Instead of strictly matching `last.id` string equality (which breaks when streaming IDs are reconciled to canonical DB IDs):
1. **Content Hash / Fingerprinting**: Track spoken messages by a hash of `(message.text, message.createdAt)` or `contentHash`.
2. **ID Reconciliation**: Update `lastSpokenIdRef` when a message object in `$messages` is updated from a temporary ID to a canonical database ID.

### Environment

- Platform: Desktop (Electron / Webview)
- Hermes Version: Latest main / desktop app
- TTS Provider: Custom / Plugin TTS (e.g., OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint)

items.title: Desktop build fails: CLI forces CI=1, electron-builder then attempts implicit publishing and aborts

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

`hermes update` / `hermes desktop` cannot build the desktop app on a source install: the CLI forces `CI=1` for the npm lifecycle, electron-builder 26.15.3 reads that as "running in CI", enables **implicit publishing**, and then hard-fails resolving a publish configuration that a local `--dir` build never needed.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13), source install
- Linux x64 (Ubuntu), Node via the Hermes-managed toolchain
- `apps/desktop` at 0.17.0, electron-builder 26.15.3, Electron 40.10.2

## What happens

```
→ Building desktop packaged app...
  • electron-builder  version=26.15.3 os=...
  • Implicit publishing triggered by CI detection. This behavior will be disabled in electron-builder v27. Please use --publish explicitly.
  • packaging       platform=linux arch=x64 electron=40.10.2 appOutDir=release/linux-unpacked
  • copying unpacked Electron  ...
  ⨯ Cannot detect repository by .git/config. Please specify "repository" in the package.json
    failedTask=build stackTrace=Error: Cannot detect repository by .git/config...
        at getInfo (app-builder-lib/src/publish/PublishManager.ts:608:13)
        at getResolvedPublishConfig (.../PublishManager.ts:617:18)
        at resolvePublishConfigurations (.../PublishManager.ts:500:16)
        at getPublishConfigs (.../PublishManager.ts:472:10)
        at getAppUpdatePublishConfiguration (.../PublishManager.ts:265:73)
        at Packager.emitAfterPack (app-builder-lib/src/packager.ts:338:5)
npm error Lifecycle script `pack` failed with error: code 1
✗ Desktop GUI build failed
```

The app itself is packaged fine — `release/linux-unpacked/Hermes` and `resources/app.asar` are both written — the build only dies in the `afterPack` publish hook, so the failure is purely about publishing metadata.

## Root cause

1. `hermes_cli/main.py` → `_npm_lifecycle_env()` sets `"CI": "1"` in the environment used for every npm lifecycle, including the desktop `pack`.
2. `app-builder-lib/out/publish/PublishManager.js` enables implicit publishing when `publishOptions.publish === undefined` and `ci-info.isCI` is true, setting the policy to `onTagOrDraft`.
3. That policy makes `getAppUpdatePublishConfiguration` resolve a publish config, which calls `getInfo` → `getRepositoryInfo`. `apps/desktop/package.json` declares no `repository`, and `apps/desktop` has no `.git` of its own, so detection fails and the build aborts.

Worth noting as a second-order risk: with the implicit policy, `isPublish` evaluates **true** for a purely local build. A local `hermes desktop` rebuild is one resolvable repository away from attempting an upload to GitHub releases.

## Suggested fix

The `pack` script is the local/dev packaging path and never publishes by design, so make that explicit:

```diff
-    "pack": "npm run build && npm run builder -- --dir",
+    "pack": "npm run build && npm run builder -- --dir --publish never",
```

Verified locally: with `--publish never` the repository message drops to a harmless warning, the pack completes, and `hermes desktop` proceeds to launch.

(The same reasoning may apply to the other local-build scripts; `dist:*` release targets should of course keep their current behavior.)

items.title: computer-use status/install exit 0 when the driver is unusable

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

`hermes computer-use status` and `hermes computer-use install` both exit `0` when the driver is unusable. A script cannot distinguish a healthy driver from a broken one without parsing stdout.

## Reproduction

Point the override at a binary that is not cua-driver:

```powershell
$env:HERMES_CUA_DRIVER_CMD = "$env:SystemRoot\System32\cmd.exe"
hermes computer-use status
echo $LASTEXITCODE
```

Output:

```text
cua-driver: installed at C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe [custom binary from HERMES_CUA_DRIVER_CMD] (...)
  ⚠ Repair required: driver manifest is missing or invalid
    Update the binary selected by HERMES_CUA_DRIVER_CMD, or unset the override and run: hermes computer-use install --upgrade
0
```

`install` behaves the same way — it correctly refuses to run the upstream installer against an overridden path, prints the guidance, and exits `0`.

The same holds for a genuinely broken install, not just the override case: the "Repair required" branch returns without a non-zero status.

## Why it matters

This is the natural preflight in CI or a provisioning script:

```bash
hermes computer-use status || echo "driver broken"
```

It never fires. Anything gating computer-use work on driver health silently proceeds against a driver that cannot serve a session, and the failure resurfaces later as an opaque "backend unavailable" mid-run.

## Suggested change

Exit non-zero on the unusable-driver paths:

- `status`: non-zero when the runtime contract check fails ("Repair required"), and when the driver is not installed at all
- `install`: non-zero when it declines to repair (e.g. an incompatible custom binary behind `HERMES_CUA_DRIVER_CMD`)

Both currently `return` from those branches in `hermes_cli/main.py` (`cmd_computer_use`) without setting a status.

Worth deciding deliberately, since anything already scripting these commands would start seeing failures it previously ignored — which is the point, but it is a behavior change.

## Context

Found while testing Cua Driver 0.20 runtime-contract work in #87646. Left out of that PR to keep the status changes narrow.
